# THE SUBORNED · AGENT GDD v0.24.0 · 2026-10-18
src: the-suborned-gdd-v0.24.0-2026-10-18.html. On conflict the src wins; report the mismatch to Aster. §13 TESTS exists only here. §15 ART = the art bible; its machine copy contracts/style/suborned.style.json (v0.21.0: signals own no colours) wins on conflict. The v0.15.0 html art bible is history (~/Projects/the-suborned/GDD/v0.15.0/): concept look reference only; its painted presentation and palette are superseded.

## §01 GAME + CORE (loaded first by every agent)
game: single-player real-time tactics + social infiltration · PC · Unity · camera above street, never first person · exteriors only (interiors = timed off-screen actions; shops, bars and workshops are frontages) · multi-level exteriors: street 0, deck 9.43 m, sky concourse 24 m (sky rail platforms) · mission = 1 block, 8–12 min, live clock
fantasy: commander. The city carries out your plan without knowing it: turn ordinary people, time their small acts into one plan.
arc: one person → networks → districts. Every system adds to or tests that growth.
look: bright retro-future (pastel cream + peach stone, saturated enamel accents, lagoon water, coral transit, chrome; skyline of towers, rockets, planets). Optimistic surface, coercive underneath.
world (Sky, 2026-10-14): an alternate history, not a forecast: "a 1950s world that discovered atomic power centuries ago". Culture and style 1950s, technology centuries ahead ("robots have 1950's style, the trams etc, just the technology is super advanced"). Not "the 1950s imagining the year 2000". People wear the city's space-age couture, never 1950s period dress (§15 people).
- atomic power made energy, travel and building cheap (sky rail, skyports, towers, liners): everything physical is abundant.
- thinking machines and networks never came ("internet wasn't a thing"): no networked computing; robots are clockwork-smart and follow fixed routines; records are physical (microfilm, punch cards, pneumatic tubes, stamped forms). Information moves through people and paper, so people are the weak point: why the game is about suborning them (pillar subvert people; tiebreaker people > powers).
- the city fears disorder most: an abundant, orderly city runs on routine and paperwork; hence optimistic surface, coercive underneath.
- design test for every object: 1950s style, centuries-ahead technology (crossing signals float, markings need not be paint; brief 009).
- reads (rules unchanged): cameras are closed-circuit, watched by people · a watcher's log is a physical record that investigators pull · calls are voice between people (telephone, radio) · "networks" in the arc and transit = people and lines, never computers · "no AI at runtime", fight AI and AI chatter are build terms, not the world.
pillars (test):
- subvert people: does knowing more make a person cheaper, quieter or more loyal?
- orchestrate the city: does it open or close a window the player can see coming?
- live with it: will the player meet this choice again?
tiebreakers, in order: readable > rich · people > powers · systems > scripts (nothing hand-authored) · preparation > improvisation · commander > avatar · exteriors only
pace (Sky, 2026-10-15: "more realtime than strategy"): real-time play is the default; pause is a tool, not the mode. The tiebreakers stand: you still command from above and prepare before you act. Show the rules in the street, not in text (Sky, 2026-10-16: "It's the reading, it's too much"): the systems stay deep, the player reads them from people, rings, lines and locks (§10).
terms: Trail = campaign evidence from traceable acts, drives investigations · Alert 0–3 = security response now (routine, inquiry, search, lockdown) · security level S 0–4 = how hard a district answers an alarm (lax, routine, watchful, guarded, swarm): the response dial (§05) · Standing = Hero ↔ Menace per district: acts seen or found, a public fight once by opponent, and word of mouth between missions; starts leaning Hero (+2) · Heat = T + Menace, threshold schedules a fight · bravery (helped → Fighter) / resentment (coerced → Informer) · Talker = fear + resentment > bravery + loyalty, gives you up when questioned
house rules:
- build only against Keel's rulebook (each event: needs, changes, witnesses). Unknown = reject.
- no AI at runtime. Content generated at build time. Same orders → same result. Any run replays exactly from start state + orders.
- handoff = inputs · done-check · next owner.
- only Latch edits Unity scenes. Price paid runs before starting.
- escalate to Sky (via Aster) only: pillar change, new paid spend, release, destructive action, unresolved conflict.

## §02 LOOP + RESOURCES
mission: Watch → Learn → Turn → Time → Take → Fight → Inherit
campaign: turned people pay cash/arms/tips → turn more people (snowball). Contacts grow braver or bitter. T + Standing set pushback.
| resource | scope | drives | from |
| Cash | campaign | fees, debts, bribes, turning | sources (skimming clerk, bookmaker) |
| Arms | campaign | winning fights, arming joiners; how many of your people carry a gun this mission (one sidearm per point; the Enforcer's carbine is the cell's) | sources (quartermaster, hijack) |
| Assets | campaign | access, income, fight allies | Fixer, introductions |
| Time | mission | actions 3–62 s (a kill 3 s, a knockout 6 s); events don't wait | — |
| Trail | campaign | investigations; part of Heat | traceable acts: threats, visible payments, people hit by gunfire, people taken down (knockout +4, kill +6, charged when a report is confirmed or the victim gives a statement), missing persons (+2) |
| Alert 0–3 | mission | security response now | reports that land (a witness, a camera, a missed check-in, a missing person), found faults, shots |
| Security level S 0–4 | district | the response's size and speed | the district's base, its open cases, the mission (§05) |
| Standing | district | who agrees, crowd behaviour | acts seen or found, public fights, word of mouth (§04) |
rule: every order shows its full price before commit ($, time, T, A risk, who would see it). In real time: one line per way on the action panel, the move ring on the ground, Alt for the breakdown, the going-loud card (§10).
travel [S]: boarding a tram or sky rail is fast travel round the city: board at any stop or station, ride to any other on the network. Price = time only: wait for the next service + the ride, both from the timetable. No fare.
chain: Handover route A is itself a chain (watch café → clear Inez's debt → loop camera → coffee spill pulls guard → take Vale). Each person sees only their part; city investigates backward, link by link [S]. Later operations chain more links across a district [L].

## §03 CELL
| op | verbs | notes |
| Scout | Watch, Listen, Mislead | Watch reveals a routine, and a watcher's sight (its cone) and check-in marks; Listen reveals need and temperament; false tips send rivals away; fires as untrained |
| Fixer | Turn, Call | offer/pay/help/threaten; calls contacts in on cue; the face witnesses remember; fires as untrained |
| Tech | Loop, Reroute | blinds surveillance, misdirects patrols; tethered while holding; fires as untrained |
| Enforcer | Enter, Take, Takedown, Fire | the only op who knocks out or kills in silence (§06) and who carries Vale; carries the carbine |
all ops [S]: any op can carry a sidearm (one per Arms point) and Fire (§06). Every op can run (double-click, or G on a moving op) at 2.8 m/s, twice the walk, and is noticed (§05). Any op can carry a body (the Enforcer at the walk, 1.4 m/s; the others at 0.7 m/s), put it down (1 s), restrain a living one (8 s) and stash it (§05 bodies). Nobody runs while carrying Vale, a downed op or a body, while tethered or mid-action; nobody fires while running or carrying.
training: full cell. campaign: starts Fixer only; recruit the rest by turning people with the skill [S].

## §04 PEOPLE
person = routine + need + temperament + memory. Knowledge lowers price; standing decides who listens.
approaches (Inez, training) [B]:
| approach | requires | $ | time | T | leaves |
| Ask cold | — | 0 | 25 s | +1 | remembered refusal: later offers +$10,000, +1 T |
| Pay | routine known (Watch 20 s [S]; was 52 s [B]) | 70,000 | 50 s | +2 | traceable payment; neutral |
| Help (clear debt) | need known (Listen 42 s) | 40,000 | 50 s | +1 | gratitude; bravery can grow |
| Pressure | need known | 0 | 35 s | +3 | fear; resentment grows; can identify Fixer |
purse: pay + driver = 110,000 > 100,000; help + driver = 80,000 fits → learning buys the second route.
private [S] (Sky, 2026-10-16: "seeing someone being turned isn't a concern. That's too much, would consider the conversation private, unless it's pressure"): Ask, Pay, Help and Listen have no witnesses: onlookers learn nothing, so they add no witness Trail, no Standing, no incident and nothing told along ties. The approach's own price stands (its Trail, time and cash; Pay is still traceable money; a Loyal subject still reports an approach). Pressure is not private: a threat is seen, remembered and passed on.
temperament [S]:
| type | responds to | Hero | Menace |
| Idealist | Help; refuses bribes | volunteers free; bravery fast | refuses; may report |
| Mercenary | Pay | overcharges | discount; sells you to highest bidder |
| Fearful | Pressure | hesitates; needs Help ×2 | folds free |
| Loyal (institution) | trust over time | turns after repeated Help | reports any approach |
Hero and Menace campaigns turn different halves of the city = replay value.
bravery [S]: Informant → Helper → Accomplice (hides op, drives) → Fighter (joins armed). +1 step per job completed unexposed.
resentment [S]: Compliant → Resentful → Informer (sells a route → ambush scheduled later). +1 step per pressure or exposure.
talker [S]: questioned, a person gives up known facts if fear + resentment > bravery + loyalty (deterministic). Facts: saw the Fixer's face, saw the Enforcer's face (a witness of a takedown, or a victim who saw him coming), knows cell car, saw where/when. A person who reported volunteers place and time. Brave helped contact lies → nothing or false lead.
scales [S]: every number reads as a word: bravery informant·helper·accomplice·fighter (0–3) · resentment compliant·resentful·informer (0–2) · fear calm·uneasy·afraid·terrified (0–3) · loyalty none·obliged·trusting·sworn (0–3). Loyalty in the talker test = loyalty to the cell, 0 at start; loyalty to an employer or the civic order is the Loyal temperament. Start: everyone 0, except Idealist bravery 1 (helper) and Fearful fear 1 (talks when questioned until helped).
wrong approach [S]: an approach that doesn't suit the temperament still works one step worse (one more Help, or a higher price; Keel sets the numbers); an approach the temperament refuses (Pay to an Idealist) fails and leaves a remembered refusal.
preview: an order always shows its price; whether it will work shows as "?" until Listen reveals the temperament (Sky, 2026-10-15: Watch gives where and when; Listen gives who they are).
needs [S]: one clear need per person from a closed list: debt · cash · housing · papers · kin · care · protection · advancement · secret. Each is met by Help or Pressure; a need that requires something (kin: a family tie; protection: a rival tie; advancement: work) is checked in the data. A met need is replaced between missions, drawn from the person's own stream (id + mission number); a turned contact tells it free in the debrief, anyone else needs Listen again.
ties [S]: family ≤ 4 · workmate ≤ 3 (same employer) · regular ≤ 3 out, 12 in (their routine stops at the unit while its staff are on shift) · debtor ≤ 2 owed, 6 in · rival ≤ 1 (same trade or employer); 1–8 per person, nobody isolated, nobody a hub. Introductions travel only along family, workmate and regular ties.
knowledge [S]: a person knows a fact only if they witnessed it (clear sightline within 13 m, §05) or were told it along a tie: face to face within 20 m, or by phone to a tie indoors (calls are voice, §01); a told fact is never told on. At the start nobody knows anything about the cell, and the cell is known by face only (no alias [L]). A keeper knows the needs of their workmates and regulars (§08 tips). Facts travel along ties, never opinion; the one feeling that travels is the word of a person the cell helped or harmed, between missions (standing, below).
restricted [S]: guards, patrol officers and investigators are Loyal or Mercenary; councillors, watchers, pawnbrokers and credit bureaux are never Idealist. Every trade and role carries ≥ 2 temperaments; no temperament over 60 % of a cast row; a unit of ≥ 3 staff carries ≥ 2.
between missions: promoted (new access) · arrested (lost unless freed) · introduces a friend (new contact) · comes home after a knockout and gives a statement (unless quieted) · grieves a found killing (a turned contact takes the saw-violence move; other family, lover and workmate ties fear +1) · worries for a missing person (those ties fear +1) · tells their ties how the cell treated them (standing). Debrief reports each with cause.
standing [S]: per district, an integer; Hero band at +3 or more, Menace band at −3 or less. Every district starts at +2, leaning Hero (Sky, 2026-10-16: "Hero is kinda the default, if you're not seen then everyone assumes you're good (it's that kinda world)"), one known kindness short of the band.
- in a mission only acts seen or found move it: −1 per seen incident of a threat (Pressure), violence, a drawn weapon, a takedown or a carry; −1 for a found killing, even unseen; a missing person 0.
- a public fight (city people within 30 m of any shot; it ends 30 s after the last shot, or with the final fight) moves it once, when it ends, by opponent: fired on the guard, patrol, officers or robots −1; fired first on rivals the district does not fear −1; broke rivals the district fears +1 (Sky: "a rival gang that has menace level authority is a +1"); anything else 0. How the public sees a mission's rivals is mission data (the Handover's: feared); a district default comes later, with the campaign.
- between missions, word of mouth (Sky: "if you help in a good way then can move to hero"): each person the cell Helped tells their ties (+1); each it Pressured or knocked out tells of the harm (−1); once per person, not per tie; helped and harmed counts as harmed; at most ±2 per district per mission. The word is a feeling, not a fact: no face, place or time, nothing for investigators.
- drift: a district nothing moved this mission moves 1 step back toward +2, from either side.
Hero: help people (their word), shield civilians, drive off feared rivals in public, free arrested locals. Menace: shoot in crowds, public threats, harm bystanders, fight the police, a killing found. An unseen threat moves Standing only through the victim's word. Neither end loses.
| | Hero | Menace |
| turning | slower, dearer, loyal | faster, cheaper, betrayal risk |
| crowds | join fights, hide ops | obey from fear, report, scatter under fire |
| fights | fewer; police hesitate in crowds | more often; harder |
| street | graffiti, cheering, free tips | wanted posters, averted eyes, empty pavements |

## §05 PRESSURE
urgency = scheduled events with reasons, never an arbitrary countdown. Each mission defines its closing event.
security: the door guard's routine (café stop pre-shift) [B] · every staff post (guards, patrol officers, watchers) checks in by voice every 90 s from the start of its shift, and at its end; a missed mark is a report that lands at the mark, Alert 1 [S] · cameras: fixed cones, blocked by roofs/parked vehicles, on a screen a person scans every 20 s [S] · the player sees a watcher's cone only once the Scout has watched it; a watcher not yet watched shows "?" and still sees you (§03, §10) [S] · patrol sweep, breaks to gunfire within 30 m [B] · the response comes by the dial (below); the district seals the level's seal time after the later of a confirmation at Alert ≥ 2 and the response on the street (2:25 at S1 and S2) [S].
rivals [B]: same target, own schedule. False tip: away 3:50. Gunfire: arrive within 16 s.
| A | security does | raised by |
| 0 routine | follows schedules | — |
| 1 inquiry [S] | robots check the spot; patrol tightens | a landed report of a found knockout, a woken victim, a noise, a missed check-in, a missing person; a found fault; once per incident |
| 2 search [B] | the response unit and robots to the place; the search opens stashes within 30 m | a 2nd incident; a landed report of a found kill or a carry seen; any gunfire at once (sets A ≥ 2; no per-shot +1 A) |
| 3 lockdown [B] | doors lock (S2 and up); cordon units at the district mouths; district seals | a landed report of a takedown seen; gunfire or violence seen by a civilian at once |
alert rule [S]: silent acts (a takedown, a carry, a body, a missing person) raise Alert when a report lands, never at sight; gunfire at once, because security hears it. Witness Trail and Standing still move at sight. A knockout found or woken never raises Alert above 1 (a takedown seen is 3 on landing, knockout or not). One takedown is one incident and one dispatch, however many find it.
witness [S]: clear sightline within 13 m of a traceable act → +1 T per incident, moves standing. Turning is private (§04): Ask, Pay, Help and Listen have no witnesses. A turned witness (loyalty ≥ 1) adds no witness Trail for a takedown or a carry and makes no report. Crowds also block guard/camera sightlines.
reports [S]: a fact reaches security only through a person (no networks, §01). Whoever notices a takedown, a carry or a body reacts by the first row that holds: (1) a person turned for this very act (the driver who brought the car): never its witness · (2) staff: radio from where they stand (lands in 5 s) · (3) kin of the victim (lover, family): report at once · (4) turned (loyalty ≥ 1): keep quiet · (5) an Informer: report · (6) terrified: flee, never report · (7) Loyal: report · (8) Idealist: walk over to check the body, then report · (9) Mercenary: keep quiet until Alert 2, then report · (10) Fearful: flee an act, avoid a body, tell a tie. A reporter walks to the nearest report point (a staffed door, or a call box: the world places them so every street point is within 40 m of one), running after an act and walking after a body, and calls (6 s); the report lands. A live camera's lands at its next scan + 3 s; a robot's in 4 s. A reporter taken down before the report lands drops it. Whoever quiets, avoids, flees or reports also tells one tie: face to face within 20 m, or by phone to a tie indoors. No Tech action cuts a call box.
bodies [S] (Sky, 2026-10-16: "civilians can see bodies. They don't disappear; the enforcer has to take them into a quiet place"): a person knocked out or killed stays where they fell until moved; kills are shown, not cut away. An open body is found by anyone within 13 m on a clear line and by watchers in their cones. Only a stash hides one: a container (5 s on the street, seen as a carry; holds 1) or a service door (10 s, off-screen; holds 3). A container is emptied on a round every 15:00, its time learnable by Watch, in the mission only. A knocked-out victim wakes after 2:00, staggers 4 s and reports the assault (Alert 1; his facts become leads); hidden, he calls out every 10 s, heard within 20 m; restrained, he is silent until freed. On landing: a found knockout 1, a found kill 2, a carry seen 2, a takedown seen 3. A found body, knocked out or killed, brings a unit of officers at any Alert and holds the scene: the door the body lies at and every door within 13 m in sight of it refuse Enter and any exit until the unit stands down (1:00 after the last alarm at Alert 1, 3:00 at Alert 2, never at Alert 3). A body moved before the unit arrives makes the report unfounded: Alert stays, no seal. At Alert ≥ 2 the unit's search opens every stash within 30 m (10 s each). Preparation earns the right to leave a body: with the camera looped and the patrol rerouted, nobody may find it in time (Sky).
suspicion [S] (Sky: a person who expects someone and finds them missing grows suspicious and can raise the alarm): a person due to meet a lover, family member or workmate at a stop they share (from routines, never authored) who is there without them raises a missing-person alarm after 20 s (Alert 1). A turned waiter says nothing; a person being Taken reports nothing.
response [S] (Sky: "it's easy to swarm the play area with robots if we need to temper the game play"): a dial, data per district and mission, not code. S = the district's base (data in the plan) + ⌊open cases ÷ 2⌋ (at most +2) + the mission's bonus. The Handover runs at S2.
| S | name | dispatch | Alert 1 sends | Alert ≥ 2 sends | +1 unit every | unit cap | seal | Alert 3 adds |
| 0 | lax | 20 s | 1 robot | 1 unit | — | 1 | 3:00 | — |
| 1 | routine | 12 s | 1 robot | 1 unit | — | 1 | 2:25 | — |
| 2 | watchful | 10 s | 2 robots | 1 unit + 2 robots | 40 s | 3 | 2:25 | +1 unit, doors lock |
| 3 | guarded | 8 s | 2 robots | 2 units + 2 robots | 30 s | 4 | 2:00 | +1 unit, doors lock |
| 4 | swarm | 6 s | 3 robots | 2 units + 4 robots | 20 s | 6 | 1:30 | +2 units, doors lock |
A unit is 2 officers; a robot is an armed patrol unit, and robots count against the 30-combatant cap. An alarm sends the response to the scene, then to where the missing person's post, car and close ties are meant to be now, then to the alarm-raiser's ties (up to 3 each); robots go only to places within 60 m of where they start. Fighting out is a last resort, not a route (Sky).
running [S]: a runner is noticed where an act would be: people with a clear line within 13 m, and the cones of the guard, patrol, live cameras, response unit and rivals. People remember where and when (and the Fixer's face if he ran): a lead, no T, no standing. Security that sees a runner counts a found fault: A ≥ 1, once per run; a guard who saw a runner no longer fights at your side. Running is free once a fight is on, the run is loud, or the op is under fire.
drawn weapon [S]: seen by security → A ≥ 2 and that watcher engages (reacts 2 s, then fires); seen by people within 13 m → one witnessed incident (+1 T, A ≥ 1), and they remember the face; unseen costs nothing.
alarm inside [S]: once A ≥ 2 the target's building hides them: Enter +30 s (Handover 38 → 68 s).
levels [S]: street, deck and sky concourse are all exterior. Sightlines and the 13 m run in 3D: a slab blocks sight straight up and down, an open edge does not. People change level only by stair, ramp, escalator or lift (time from the plan). Watchers stand per level; a station watcher covers its concourse.
watchers [S]: cameras and civic robots stand at key places on the district plan (stations, stops, gates, squares). Any op in a watcher's sightline is logged with place + time, act or no act. Once a Trail is open, investigators can pull the log: each sighting is a lead (place + time). Hot (Heat over threshold, Motive sets it) or Menace standing in the district: a sighting counts as a witness report (Alert table).
investigators [S][L]: on foot question ~every 20 s; cars move fast, stop to question; count rises with A and T. Pick civilians near last incident by sightline + distance, not luck. Useful answer = fact with place + time → go there, question again; ~60–90 s per hop.
visible: questioning icon, dotted line joining held leads, unit following it.
counters: keep moving (sightings go stale) · reach witness first (pay/reassure/threaten; threat adds fear) · Scout false tip · citizens block cars · break sightlines in a crowd.
output: findings → debrief Investigation state → next mission. Hero campaign: brave locals give false leads.

## §06 FIGHTS
fights measure preparation (arms, brave contacts, streets). Not a separate combat game: fast and real-time, Syndicate-like; a fight is short, lethal and decided by what you prepared.
frequency [S]: Heat = campaign T + Menace standing. Threshold crossed → fight event (raid, ambush, rival hit) in next mission. No dice.
The security level S (§05) is a separate axis: Heat brings fights to the cell; S makes a district watch harder.
size [S]: act I 3–6 hostiles · II 8–15 · III 20–30. Hard cap 30 simulated combatants; rest = background crowd (run/cheer only).
your side: cell + Accomplice/Fighter contacts + crowd joiners (Hero), armed up to Arms stock.
citizen actions: scatter (breaks sightlines, covers retreat) · block (lorry, stalled tram, crowd vs police vehicles) · join (bare-handed or armed) · vehicle strike (ram barricade or rigged vehicle; driver always jumps clear).
content line: civilians are never the payload; no coerced suicide attacks. Menace can be uglier (collateral, witnesses) but no civilian dies as the weapon.
health [S]: civilian 2 · guard/officer 3 · rival 3 · patrol unit 4 · Scout/Fixer/Tech 4 · Enforcer 6. Pips on select and over all in a fight. Weapons (Arms): pistol 1 dmg, heavier 2–3. Armour via quartermaster, healing via turned doctor (people, not upgrades).
armed [S]: any op can carry a sidearm (pistol), one per Arms point; the Enforcer's carbine is the cell's and uses none. The Enforcer stays the heavy (carbine, health 6, the only one who carries Vale). The Handover issues all four; the campaign starts with the Fixer alone and Arms 0.
takedown [S] (Sky, 2026-10-16: "in theory can take out anyone, but it's all about being seen or not … Killing a civilian in front of a camera as a lone gunman is highly likely to end in failure"): anyone on the street can be targeted; there is no named list, and the cost comes only from who sees it. The Enforcer, within 1.5 m, knocks a person out (6 s) or kills them (3 s), silently: no gunfire rule applies, no money. A target who sees him coming (or witnessed one of the cell's acts this mission) is aware: unarmed, he struggles (+3 s), screams (heard within 20 m) and holds the Enforcer's face; armed, the takedown fails and it is a fight. Knockout: the victim wakes and talks unless hidden, restrained or turned. Kill: never talks, but a found body is far worse (§05, §08). Not targets: the patrol robot and cameras (Reroute and Loop are their verbs). Vale: a kill fails the mission; a knockout is refused (use Take).
| weapon [S] | dmg | every | point blank | effective | long |
| pistol | 1 | 1.5 s | ≤ 5 m: 1000 ‰ | ≤ 15 m: 750 ‰ | ≤ 25 m: 400 ‰ |
| carbine | 2 | 2.0 s | ≤ 5 m: 1000 ‰ | ≤ 20 m: 750 ‰ | ≤ 30 m: 400 ‰ |
modifiers [S] (multiply, ‰): shooter walking 500 · target still beside cover 500 · Enforcer holding Vale 750 · untrained (Scout, Fixer, Tech, rivals) 750; Enforcer, officers and the guard are trained. No reload or ammunition: Arms is the limit. Draw 1.0 s, holster 0.5 s, first shot on a new target 1.0 s; a hostile surprised outside a fight reacts in 2.0 s.
hits [S]: deterministic, a hit rate, not a roll: each shooter keeps an integer accumulator per target (starts 500, + accuracy per shot, a hit at 1000). Shown as "hits 3 in 4 · down in n s"; the cursor shows the band by shape. No dice.
orders [S]: fire (until the target is down; holds aim 3 s if the line breaks; walking keeps firing at the walking rate, running cancels it) · cease · stance: hold (fires only when ordered), return (default on draw: fires at whoever fires on this op), at will (fires at any combatant in reach, nearest first) · panic: every armed op draws and goes to at will, only once a fight is on. Combatant = a final-fight hostile, or anyone who has fired on or aims at the cell; never a civilian, contact, Vale, or a guard or patrol that hasn't engaged, so only an explicit fire starts a loud run. Group focus fire = one fire order to every selected op.
cost [S]: per person, not per shot: +2 T per person hit (once), +2 T more if they go down (a dropped guard = 4 T). A takedown costs the same per person without the gunfire: knockout +4 T, kill +6 T, charged when a report of it is confirmed or the victim gives a statement; a kill never found is a missing person (+2 T, §08); any gunfire → A ≥ 2 (§05); violence seen by a civilian → 3. Shots in the final fight are untraced (no T, no A; Sky, 2026-10-15); shots before it count. Gunfire still calls the response unit, draws rivals in 16 s, breaks the patrol within 30 m, moves Menace if witnessed. Shooting a contact ends the relationship. Shooting the target = fail.
hostiles [S] (Pulse): advance to the nearest free cover point (made at build time) toward their objective (the getaway car in the final fight, else where they last saw the cell); engage when a foe is in effective reach. Target priority: whoever shoots at them → whoever holds Vale → nearest armed op → nearest op; never Vale, never a civilian. Rivals break when more than half are down; police hold. Crowds within 30 m of gunfire scatter.
downed: op at 0 = downed; carry (3 s; the carrier walks and doesn't fire) to the car, or captured → rescue mission.
civilians targetable: anyone can be targeted (takedown). Violence on a civilian seen by anyone → −1 Standing per incident, on top of the fight's own move (§04); a contact who witnesses it loses bravery and gains fear and resentment → some Informer, more Talkers. Fastest way to undo progress.
prototype [B] (history, superseded by the rules above): Enforcer shot 6 s; 2 hits drop a person or patrol unit; Enforcer takes 3. Each shot +1 A, +2 T, draws rivals + patrols, Menace if witnessed.
decisive shot [L]: 1–2× per fight: slow time, camera behind Enforcer, one aimed shot, back to tactical.

## §07 HANDOVER (training mission · capstone)
brief: Councillor Vale signed the clearance order for the marked block. At shift handover he leaves the Civic Records Office for his official car. Take him alive to the getaway car. Full cell, all four armed (Arms 3). Purse $100,000. Every verb introduced once.
cast: Vale · Inez (café waitress, in debt; secretly the door guard's lover) · the door guard (Inez's lover; his pre-shift café stop is to see her) · official driver (needs cash) · the Office's other guards (official entrance; the relief at 5:30) · rival crew (feared by the public) · cameras · patrol. The Handover runs at security level S2.
the capstone (Sky, 2026-10-15: "the guard comes to visit Inez when she calls him because you bribed / pressured her and that's what makes him leave his post"): the call that pulls the guard off his door is Inez, called because the cell helped, paid or pressured her. Her debt is her need (Help clears it); the affair is her secret (Pressure threatens to expose it).
casting: the mission names roles (employer, position, place, shift, need, approach; the guard a café regular), and rule M-2 casts each from the city's generated people and pins it by id; "Inez" and "Vale" are pinned name parts given to whoever is cast (contracts/missions/handover/mission.json; brief 010).
schedule: 0:00 Vale inside; routines run; the cell stands loosely by the getaway car at the square's boarding pavilion, in view, and the camera opens on them · the door guard checks in at 1:00, 2:30, 4:00 and 5:30 (shift end; other staff posts keep 90 s marks from their own shift start) · 3:10 rival car parks near pickup · 5:30 handover chime · 5:40 last chance to turn driver · 5:50 Vale exits north (service lane if driver turned) · 6:10 Vale at car · 8:30 rivals take Vale or car leaves = over.
route A, front door (before 5:50): Scout watches café, listens to Inez (1:34) → Fixer helps Inez ($40,000) → Tech loops entrance camera (1:02, tethered; optional patrol reroute 1:55) → Fixer calls Inez: guard walks 30 s, stays 60 s, returns 30 s = 2:00 window [payoff cut] → Enforcer enters (38 s), exits service door with Vale, to car (44 s).
route B, pickup (from 5:50): Scout watches car: driver needs cash (48 s) → Fixer turns driver before 5:40 ($40,000): pickup moves to service lane, or driver blocks pickup camera 2:30 → Scout false tip on rivals (44 s), or fight → Enforcer intercepts (38 s), to car (44 s).
route G, the guard [S] (brief 013): Tech loops the entrance camera and reroutes the patrol → Scout watches the guard (his cone and check-in marks) → Enforcer knocks him out just after a mark, then leaves him, or carries him out of the door's sight if a finder could come while the cell still needs the door → enters, out by the service door with Vale, to the car (G-fast 3:36, $0, 6 T, Alert 1). No guard ally in the final fight. Kill variant: kill, stash in the lane's container or through the service door, beat the container's round; debrief: a missing person, an open case, the Office block hardens.
the driver [S]: takeable by the rules (Sky), but not viable on the generated cast: every time he could be taken is closed by check-ins, the shift change or Vale himself (Waymark, c012). Turn him instead (route B). The official car needs its driver: with no driver it waits.
the Take [S] (Sky): at Vale's own car with his driver turned, the Take happens inside the car, off-screen, with nothing to witness. Any other Take has a 5 s struggle onlookers can see. Escorted on foot, Vale looks wrong only to his kin, or to anyone within 3 m who sees the grip.
timings [S]: walking legs shorten where the cell runs (Waymark retimes the routes); the Enforcer walks while carrying Vale. Once A ≥ 2, Enter takes 68 s (alarm inside, §05); a held door refuses Enter (§05 bodies).
final fight [S]: always; 30–60 s (Sky, 2026-10-17, as the rulebook has it); 3–5 hostiles; its shots are untraced (§06).
- loud (any shot or A ≥ 2): police from the north street (the top-down test's west street, as built), 2–4 officers, plus the response unit if it is on the street; seal clock running, no allies.
- safe (no shots, A ≤ 1): rivals ambush extraction; guard (never saw you, never taken down) fights them; helped Inez warns 10 s early; turned driver blocks rival car (−1 rival); earlier false tip (−1 rival).
win: Vale alive at getaway car.
fail: Vale killed · Vale leaves in official car · rivals reach Vale · district seals · Enforcer down · entry seen by guard, live camera or patrol. Withdraw ends the attempt. A takedown seen by a live camera is not an instant fail: it is reported (Alert 3 on landing).
reference results (c015, start Standing +2; Standing at the end → after the word): A Help ×2 4:22.8 · $80,000 · 5 T · A 1 · +3 → +4 · A Pressure 3:29.9 · $0 · 7 T · A 1 · +2 → +1 · B driver paid 7:39.3 · $70,000 · 3 T · A 0 · +3 · G 4:07.4 · $0 · 6 T · A 1 · +3 → +2 · G-fast 3:35.9 · 6 T · A 1 · +3 → +2 · G-kill 4:44.3 · 2 T + 2 missing, 1 open case · A 1 · +3 · loud 4:23.5 · 13 T · A 2 · 0. Privacy cut A's Trail from 7 to 5 and B's from 4 to 3.
reference case: the mission generator must reproduce a mission of Handover's quality; the checker must pass it.

economy [S]: turned people become sources paying each mission: clerk skims cash, quartermaster diverts arms, café owner tips needs before Scout listens. Procurement missions target a source. Snowball.
wounds [S]: health carries over. Turned doctor heals fast and quietly. No doctor → optional pre-mission objective to watch/turn/pay one, if calendar allows. Main mission date never moves. Choice: go in hurt, short-handed, or spend the days.
objectives [S]: kidnapping · bank job via planted teller · killing by manipulated proxy · takeover via ruined reputation. Direct force always works, with bigger T.
debrief [B] → next mission:

| public security | Calm → Raised → High | final A; any shot fired |
| investigation | little → early → active (named cause) | T 0 / 1–2 / 3+; named witnesses take precedence |

## §09 GENERATION

| missions | template (objective, target, closing event, fight trigger) + district people; each mission carries its security bonus and how the public sees its rivals (feared or neutral) | mission checker |
| dialogue, portraits, voices | person data + state (brave, resentful, promoted) | tone + rating filters; sampled review |
| district plans | Datum (roads, transit, plots, gates, levels, megastructures, frontage program) + Vantage (block layouts) inside plan.standards | plan checker exit 0 (bun tools/plan/cli.ts) |

mission checker: ships only if ≥ 2 quiet routes win · loud route exists and costs more T · every fail condition reachable · no single contact essential · fully informed player finishes ≥ 1:00 before closing event. An open case counts as 3 T.
risk: sameness (Watch Dogs: Legion). Fix: history, not backstory; people are memorable via what the systems record. Text = light layer. Every field a person carries names the rule that reads it; a field nothing reads is rejected (Legion's bios changed nothing). Simulated people carry state; background people carry a routine only, so investigators question simulated people only; crowds still add T, A and standing. Live AI chatter [L] only if it never touches rules.

camera: tactical view from above, play zoom 14 at 38°, never first person; it turns in quarter steps, so yaw is 30, 120, 210 or 300 (Sky, 2026-10-17; brief 016). The mission opens with the camera framed on the cell. Capstone = 3D world built from the plan (DecoKit kit where it counts, procedural fill to the same bar); rules unchanged. Painted plates [L] optional extra at most. Characters 40–60 px tall at 1080p (job, silhouette, facing readable). Levels: architecture above the selected person's level ghosts (§15: 0.2, keeping 0.4 of its shadow).
views (Sky, 2026-10-18: "yeah try H"; briefs/011/vantage/door-recheck.json): the opening view is yaw 30 · the Records Office front is played at yaw 210, two quarter turns from the opening view: the public door, its approach, South walkway, patrol-b, the patrol sweep, the cabinet, the service lane and the service door are all in view there (at yaw 30 the public door is behind the Office's wings and shows only through the fade) · the visibility rule V-1 measures each mission point from the heading it is played at, past architecture, without the fade: 45 of the Handover's 47 points are clear; Behind café (the Scout's seat) and patrol-reroute are hidden by design.
split: built world (generated from the plan at build time, fixed in play) = buildings, paving, structures, street furniture, skyline. Live 3D state = people, vehicles, doors, surveillance, barricades, posters, anything with state. One material + light standard for both; match lighting on 1 character + 1 vehicle before building more.
controls (Sky, 2026-10-15; briefs/011/play/HOW-TO-PLAY.md, briefs/011/motive-fights.md §2.5; rotation 2026-10-17, brief 016): left click selects an agent or moves the selection (Shift adds); box-drag selects · right click a person or object opens the action panel: every action the cell can take on that target, grouped by agent, each with its full price; locked rows give their reason · with a verb picked on 1–4, right click fires it directly · right click empty ground cancels · double-click runs; G (or a click on the agent's walk/run glyph) switches a moving agent between walk and run · a moving agent's destination shows as a numbered pin; Alt shows the walk paths · right click a person with the Enforcer: Knock out and Kill are two rows of the panel · hold Alt for detail · I opens Intel, L or the notes key the history, R the response list, H hides hints · the briefing (until Begin) and the end card are modal: nothing in the street answers the mouse or keys under them (Sky, 2026-10-16) · buttons carry no keycaps; a key is taught by the hint the first time it matters · WASD, arrow keys, middle-drag pan; the wheel zooms within the 40–60 px limit · Q/E turn the view 90° about the screen centre's ground point; Alt + middle-drag turns freely and snaps to the nearest quarter on release; the plot scope turns with the view (heading-up, a north wedge on its rim) · F1–F4, a portrait click or Tab selects an agent; a double-tap centres on them · Space pauses (tactical pause, a tool; T1), =/− change speed, N jumps to the next event · fights: F draws or holsters (the cursor becomes a crosshair); with weapons drawn, right click a hostile fires until down (hold and sweep to retarget); X ceases; V cycles the stance; Ctrl + right click for a civilian or contact; both buttons together = panic (only in a fight) · bindings remappable from one table.
price before commit, in real time [S] (brief 014):
- one line per way: the verb, then only the fields that aren't zero, in a fixed order: $ · time (walk + act, one number) · Trail · Alert · eye (open = seen, shut = unseen, ? = a watcher not yet watched) · what it teaches · carry pace · answer (✓ works, ✗ refused, ½ not yet, ? unknown). A takedown line marks the numbers that apply only if the body is found with the "found" glyph. For example: "Knock out · 7 s · (found) +4 · ▲1 · eye shut". Alt shows the zero fields and the breakdown.
- the move ring (Sky: the chip "everywhere the mouse goes is annoying"; Glyph's variant A): a ring on the ground at the cursor replaces the chip; its rim fills clockwise with the walk time (a full ring = 60 s). Safe: turquoise with footprints. Seen: the watcher's colour with an open eye, and the exposed stretch of the route glows. Unknown: cream, dashed, with a "?" eye. Raises Alert: a dark double rim with the lamp. No digits; Alt adds the numbers beside it.
- the going-loud card: the first order that would make a run loud (a draw someone will see, a fire before a fight is on, a panic with no fight) shows icons and numbers only: Alert to 2 (3 with the civilians watching), who comes and when, the seal time, what the final fight loses (crossed badges), +2 T per person hit and per person dropped; commit by holding the same input 0.5 s while the game runs (a ring fills), release or Esc cancels; never shown once a fight is on. After it, a per-target chip only.
HUD (Sky, 2026-10-15 and 10-16; briefs 011, 014): simple, Syndicate-style, built for real time. No sentences in play except people speaking (Sky: "It's the reading, it's too much"): everything else is an icon, a number, a ring or a line.
- at rest: the roster of 4 portraits (health pips, an inner selection ring; a busy chip with the act's glyph, a bar and the seconds left; the walk/run glyph on a moving agent's chip) · the selected agent's order plate (1–4) · the status pill (clock, a pause glyph, the next mark with "?" while unknown, $, Trail, Alert lamps) · the known-people discs under the pill (the mission's key people, filled once known; a click finds them) · the plot scope, bottom left · the notes (history) key, bottom right, with an unread dot · at most two icons over a person. The dock and finish are closed as built (Sky, 2026-10-17): round 4 v10's signage kit, the roster in the left column; the dock stays a setting.
- lines: the goal line, bottom centre: one imperative, its key noun coloured as its marker ("Take ▼Vale alive."; 6 s, back at the chime and at Vale's exit); the hint shares that place (≤ 6 words, retired for good once its verb is used). Story beats only, lower right: ≤ 2, 4 s each, ≤ 4 words ("Inez called the guard.", "Body found.", "Police coming."), and none while the speaker's own bubble is on screen. Speech bubbles at the speaker (≤ 2, 3 s, ≤ 10 words). Refusals: one pop of an icon and ≤ 4 words ("Too far · 4 m", "Watch first").
- world markers (told and learned only): eye (open, shut or ? over a watcher, and over an armed takedown's target) · wake ring on a knocked-out body, emptying to the wake · lock on a held door, with its countdown ring · "!" and a dotted line: a witness walking to the phone · clock pip over a watched guard: the time to his next check-in · "?" over a watcher not yet watched · cones: learned only, one at a time (the focused watcher's), Alt shows every learned cone · stash plates · carry disc, unit badges · objective marks and edge arrows.
- the plot scope (Sky: "Minimap may be the key though. For example knowing where Vale is located is not obvious"): a period plotting scope, about 1.5 % of the screen, showing only what the cell knows: the cell's discs; Vale's last known place as a ring that grows with the age of the information (exact only while an agent sees him); key people once met; learned cones and the patrol route; held doors, bodies, stashes, reports in transit and arriving units. Edge arrows on the main view point to Vale and anything urgent. Pan and select only; no orders from the scope.
- Alt (held): every learned mark at once, names over known people, the full fields of every price, the long lines as a second step. Nothing sticks.
- budget [S]: checked on every capture (tools/hud-budget): ≤ 15 % of the screen at rest (aim under 10 %), 22 % with an order card open, 30 % with Alt; no running text outside speech, beats and the goal line. A new mechanic says how it reads without text before it is built.
readability: cones red · guard amber · rivals violet, drawn unlit and emissive and outside the post grade, so neither light nor grade shifts them: a signal never depends on the light. Each signal has its own shape or motion cue, so it reads by shape, not by owning its colour: red, amber and violet are free for the world and props (Sky, 2026-10-16). Intel (the known-people discs and their rows: name, job, need and temperament icons; the sentences on Alt) replaces the dossier (Sky, 2026-10-17). Kills are shown: the act plays on screen and the body lies where it fell. Fights read: a tracer per shot, a miss that ends past the target (never on the body), pips over everyone in a fight, crosshair band ticks (shape, not colour) and ✕ with no line, a stance icon on the portrait, a thin 13 m ring round a conspicuous runner, the going-loud card with its held commit.
payoff cut: plan lands → brief street-level cut → same state. Capstone has one (Inez spills coffee, guard walks off). More cuts + decisive shot [L].
audio = clock: bell, café door, 5:30 handover chime · surveillance click at sweep edge · patrol sound changes when it breaks route · Alert adds music layers; fight = full score · contacts confirm calls aloud.
look: §15 ART + style contract; palette current, tuneable (Sky reviews it in the world). Retro-future city; cell = visitors from a nearby timeline (sharper, cleaner, no deco ornament) so the four read as outsiders at 50 px.

## §11 BUILD
built: top-down test of Handover (4 ops, 2 contacts, security, rivals, shooting, debrief, campaign lock; 28 scenarios pass) · Harbour District 3D world from the plan in progress (generator + export, DecoKit + procedural, Unity builder; briefs 004, 006) · city sim architecture chosen (brief 005 A).
architecture: rules separate from engine · events carry conditions, effects, witnesses · exact replay from start state + orders · Unity must pass the same 28 scenarios before it's trusted · one C# sim engine as a Unity-free library: Unity runs it live, build tools headless via dotnet; 10 Hz fixed tick, integer state, replay = orders + checksums · performance = frame rate at play zoom, not polygons: target 60 fps at 1080p on the reference machine, a 15-inch MacBook Air M4 (Mac16,13; no fan, 10-core GPU), measured warm (after several minutes of running, since it throttles) at play zoom with people, vehicles and the simulation in, by a perf harness in a development build (Redline specifies it, Latch builds it); a mid-range PC (RTX 3060-class GPU, 6-core CPU) must also pass, as a check, not the bar.
capstone, 5 weeks:
| wk | deliverable | exit |
| 1 | rules proven in top-down test | 2 routes win; loud fails at a cost [done] |
| 2 | rules in Unity; Handover in the 3D world | 28 scenarios pass in Unity |
| 3 | cell control, contacts, security, rivals, readability | first uncoached playtest |
| 4 | final fight both branches, payoff cut, Intel, event log, debrief | new-player test; freeze rules |
| 5 | tuning, fixes, audio cues; no new systems | final uncoached gate |
gate: uncoached player can state objective + fail conditions, pick an approach from something learned, explain its $/time/T cost, complete a chain, say why police vs rivals, read what next mission inherits.
cut order if late: crowd witnesses (decorative) → patrol reroute → camera-block variant → police branch (rivals only). Never cut: both routes, one payoff cut, debrief, gate test.
beyond: vertical slice (1 district, 2–3 generated missions, temperament, standing, small fights) 6–10 wks · full game (3 acts, 3 districts, fights ≤ 30) ~12 months. Replace with measured velocity after capstone.
risks: combat feel + animation (only walk/run exist) · generated sameness · playtest time. Fixed limits: 30 combatants, vehicles on lanes, 3 districts, no interiors, no first person.

## §13 TESTS (agent copy only; not in the human GDD)
default: 6 new players.
| id | question | method | pass |
| T1 | tactical pause? | same build, 6 each way | pause wins unless no-pause players explain failures as well and rate tension higher |
| T2 | loud dominates? | log first-shot time + route; re-measured with check-ins and the dial (S2) | < 25% shoot before 2:00; informed quiet runs finish faster |
| T3 | Trail readable? | ask "why is the investigation active?" | ≥ 5/6 give correct cause |
| T4 | witnesses add decisions? | A/B witnesses on/off | players route around crowds on purpose |
| T5 | kidnapping fits tone? | framing survey | cell read as resistance, not criminals |
| T6 | final fight reads as consequence? | ask "why these enemies?" | ≥ 5/6 link it to loud/quiet |
| T7 [L] | contacts memorable? | recall 1 day later | name ≥ 2 contacts + what happened |
| T8 | shoot-outs readable? | ask "why did that operative go down?" | ≥ 5/6 name the cause (outnumbered, no cover, walking, long range) |
| T9 | takedowns cost what they show? | Handover: an unseen takedown route, then the same takedown in front of a witness who reports | the unseen route wins at Alert ≤ 1; the seen one ends in failure or a loud run; ≥ 5/6 say why |
| T10 | the street reads without text? | uncoached, HUD at rest; ask "where is Vale?", "who is the waitress?", "will that walk be seen?" | ≥ 5/6 answer from the scope, the markers and the ring; no capture fails the HUD budget |

01 · THE GAME

A city you take one person at a time

In The Suborned, a city carries out your plan without knowing it. A waitress spills a coffee, a guard steps away, a driver takes a different street: each does one small thing for their own reasons, and only you see the whole. They are the Suborned, and you lead the covert cell that turns them. It starts with one favour. By the end, whole streets block the police, lorries ram barricades and crowds fight at your signal. Everyone you turned remembers how, and the city decides whether you are its heroes or its menace.

GenreReal-time tactics · social infiltration
FantasyCommander: plan from above, the city acts
Mission8–12 min on a live clock
Cell4 operatives, one verb each
ReplayHero and Menace campaigns turn different people
TouchstonesSyndicate · Desperados III · Deus Ex · Watch Dogs: Legion · Fable · Shadow of Mordor's Nemesis
Review note. This version answers review of the submitted v0.9.18. The course instructor's feedback was that the GDD read too much like a manual, not the game and the excitement of how it plays. So the GDD leads with the game: sections 01–08 are what you play, the build and the agent crew come after, technical language is kept out, and the detail agents need lives in the agentic design document. What review changed →

Three pillars, one arc

Subvert people

Learn what someone wants and how they are wired, then make an offer that fits.

Test: does knowing more about a person make them cheaper, quieter or more loyal?

Orchestrate the city

Combine contacts, routines and machines into a timed window. Later, into a street that rises on cue.

Test: does it open or close a window the player can see coming?

Live with it

Every method leaves a trace, a reputation and a relationship that grows braver or more bitter.

Test: will the player meet this choice again?

Signature moment. In training you cleared Inez's debt. Over three missions she grows braver, from tipping you off to hiding an operative. In the fourth mission the police close the street, and Inez drives the getaway car through the cordon. In a different playthrough you threatened her instead. She complied every time and grew more resentful, and in the fourth mission she is the one who told the police where you would be.

The world: the 1950s, with centuries of atomic power

The world is an alternate history, not a forecast: "a 1950s world that discovered atomic power centuries ago". Its culture and style are the 1950s; its technology is centuries ahead ("robots have 1950's style, the trams etc, just the technology is super advanced"). It is not the 1950s imagining the year 2000. People wear the city's space-age couture, never 1950s period dress (section 15).

  • What atomic power made cheap: energy, travel and building. Sky rail, skyports, towers and liners; everything physical is abundant.
  • What never came: thinking machines and networks ("internet wasn't a thing"). There is no networked computing. Robots are clockwork-smart and follow fixed routines. Records are physical: microfilm, punch cards, pneumatic tubes, stamped forms. Information moves through people and paper, so people are the weak point, and that is why the game is about suborning them (the pillar subvert people, the tiebreaker people over powers).
  • What the city fears most: disorder. An abundant, orderly city runs on routine and paperwork; that is the reason for its optimistic surface and coercive machinery.
  • The design test for every object: 1950s style, centuries-ahead technology. Crossing signals float; road markings need not be paint.
  • How the rules read in it (the rules don't change): cameras are closed-circuit, watched by people; a watcher's log is a physical record that investigators pull; calls are voice between people, by telephone or radio; the "networks" of Act II and of the trams are people and lines, never computers; "no AI during play", fight AI and AI crowd chatter are build terms, not part of the world.

Tiebreakers

  1. Readable over rich. The player can always see who saw what, what it cost and what changed.
  2. People over powers. Access and firepower come through people with motives, never generic abilities.
  3. Systems, not scripts. Nothing is hand-authored. Content is generated, then checked by simulation.
  4. Preparation beats improvisation, both in stealth and in a street fight.
  5. Commander, not avatar. The camera stays above the street. Dropping to street level is a reward, never a way to control the game.
  6. Exteriors only. Interiors are timed actions that happen off screen. Shops, bars and workshops are their frontages: shopfront, canopy, door, service bay.
  7. Many levels, all outside. Street (0), deck (9.43 m) and sky concourse (24 m, where the sky rail stops). Megastructures carry the upper levels; stairs, ramps, escalators and lifts join them.

Real time is the default. "More realtime than strategy" (Sky): the mission runs on its live clock and you play it as it runs. Pause is a tool, not the mode. The tiebreakers stand: you still command from above, and preparation still beats improvisation.

Show it in the street, not in text. "It's the reading, it's too much" (Sky): the systems stay deep, and the player reads them from people, rings, lines and locks in the world, not from panels (section 10).

02 · LOOPS

Watch, turn, time, take, inherit

Watch→Learn→Turn→Time→Take→Fight→Inherit

A chain nobody else sees

Even the training mission is a chain. Each person thinks they are solving their own problem; only you see the whole, and the city then works backward from the result, one link at a time. Later operations chain more links across a district.

What the player manages

ResourceScopeBuys or drivesComes from
CashCampaignFees, debts, bribes. Turning people.Sources (a skimming clerk, a crooked bookmaker)
ArmsCampaignWinning fights. Arming citizens who join you. How many of your people carry a gun this mission: one sidearm per point; the Enforcer's carbine belongs to the cell.Sources (a quartermaster, a hijacked shipment)
AssetsCampaignTurned people: access, income, allies in fightsThe Fixer's work, and introductions from other assets
TimeMissionEvery action takes 3–62 s (a kill 3 s, a knockout 6 s), and scheduled events keep coming—
TrailCampaignInvestigations. Fight frequency, as part of Heat.Traceable acts: threats, conspicuous payments, people hit by gunfire, people taken down (a knockout +4, a kill +6, charged when a report is confirmed or the victim gives a statement), missing persons (+2)

Every order shows its full price before you commit: cash, time, Trail, Alert risk and who would see it. In real time that is one line per way on the action panel, the move ring on the ground, Alt for the breakdown, and the going-loud card (§10).

Fast travel. Boarding a tram or the sky rail takes the cell across the city: board at any stop or station and ride to any other. It costs time only: the wait for the next service plus the ride, both from the timetable. There is no fare. Spec

03 · THE CELL

Four operatives, four verbs

Scout

Watch · Listen · Mislead. Watch reveals a routine, and a watcher's sight (its cone) and check-in marks: the cones are the Scout's skill. Listen reveals needs and temperament. Can send rivals after false tips.

Fixer

Turn · Call. Makes offers, pays, helps or threatens, then calls contacts in at the right moment. The face everyone remembers.

Tech

Loop · Reroute. Blinds surveillance and misdirects patrols, but stays tethered to the system while it holds. It was a robot in the test; the look follows the era (§10).

Enforcer

Enter · Take · Takedown · Fire. The only operative who knocks someone out or kills them in silence (§06), the only one who carries Vale, and the one with the carbine. Everyone else works to make this operative's move quiet.

Everyone can run and shoot. Any operative can carry a sidearm, one per point of Arms, and fire; the Scout, Fixer and Tech fire as untrained. Every operative can run (double-click, or G on a moving operative) at 2.8 m/s, twice the walk, and is noticed (§05). Any operative can carry a body (the Enforcer at the walk, 1.4 m/s; the others at half that), put it down, tie up a living one (8 s) and hide it (§05). Nobody runs while carrying Vale, a downed operative or a body, while tethered or in the middle of an action, and nobody fires while running or carrying. Spec

Training gives you the full cell so you learn all four verbs. The campaign starts with the Fixer alone, and recruiting the rest of the cell is the first stretch of progression. Recruits come through the same verbs: turn someone who has the skill. Spec

04 · PEOPLE

Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes.

Every person has a routine, a need, a temperament and a memory. What you learn changes the price. Your reputation changes who will even listen.

Built These values come from the top-down test, except Watch, cut from 52 s to 20 s in brief 011 (a starting value). Paying Inez plus turning the driver costs $110,000 against a $100,000 purse. Helping her plus turning the driver costs $80,000. So finding things out is what pays for a second route.

Turning is private. "Seeing someone being turned isn't a concern. That's too much, would consider the conversation private, unless it's pressure" (Sky). Asking, paying, helping and listening have no witnesses: onlookers learn nothing, so there is no witness Trail, no change in Standing and nothing passed along. The approach keeps its own price: a payment is still traceable money, and a Loyal person still reports an approach. Pressure is different: a threat is seen, remembered and passed on. Spec

A Hero campaign and a Menace campaign turn different halves of the city, so a second playthrough has a different cast. That's the replay value.

Braver or more bitter

Helped contacts get braver

Informant → Helper → Accomplice → Fighter. They rise one step after each successful job where they were not exposed. An Accomplice hides an operative or drives. A Fighter joins fights armed. Spec

Coerced contacts get bitter

Compliant → Resentful → Informer. They rise one step each time you pressure them or they are exposed. An Informer sells a route to the police or rivals, which schedules an ambush in a later mission. Spec

Talkers, not only turncoats. Every person holds facts: who saw the Fixer's face, who saw the Enforcer's (a witness to a takedown, or a victim who saw him coming), who knows the cell's car, who saw where you went and when. Someone who reported you volunteers what they saw. Questioned, a person gives up what they know when fear plus resentment outweighs bravery plus loyalty. The rule is fixed, so the same situation always gives the same answer. A contact can stop short of Informer and still fold under questioning. A brave, helped contact lies for you, and investigators get nothing or a false lead. Spec

Contacts also have lives between missions. They can be promoted (new access), arrested (lost unless freed) or introduce a friend (a new contact). Someone knocked out comes home and gives a statement unless quieted; the family and friends of someone killed grieve, and those of someone missing worry; and everyone tells their family and workmates how the cell treated them. The debrief reports each change with its cause.

What a person is made of Spec

Every number about a person reads as a word, so Intel never shows a bare score:

  • Bravery: informant · helper · accomplice · fighter. Resentment: compliant · resentful · informer.
  • Fear: calm · uneasy · afraid · terrified. Loyalty (to the cell): none · obliged · trusting · sworn. In the Talker test, loyalty means loyalty to the cell; loyalty to an employer or to the civic order is what the Loyal temperament is.
  • At the start everyone is at the bottom of every scale, except that an Idealist starts one step braver (helper) and a Fearful person starts uneasy, so they talk when questioned until someone helps them.
  • One clear need from a closed list: debt, cash, housing, papers, kin, care, protection, advancement or a secret. Each can be met by Help or Pressure. Once a need is met, a new one appears between missions, drawn from the person's own stream so it replays; a turned contact tells you it free in the debrief, and anyone else has to be listened to again.
  • Ties: family (up to 4), workmates at the same employer (up to 3), regulars, whose routine passes through a place while its staff are on shift (up to 3 out, 12 in), debtors (up to 2 owed, 6 in) and one rival. Everyone has between 1 and 8, so nobody is isolated and nobody knows everyone. Introductions travel only along family, workmate and regular ties.
  • Jobs limit temperament: guards, patrol officers and investigators are Loyal or Mercenary, never Idealist; councillors, watchers and creditors are never Idealist. No temperament makes up more than 60 % of any group, and any workplace with 3 or more staff has at least two.

The wrong approach, and what you can see first Spec

An approach that doesn't suit someone's temperament still works, one step worse: one more Help, or a higher price (Keel sets the numbers). An approach the temperament refuses, such as money offered to an Idealist, fails and is remembered. Before you commit, the order always shows its full price; whether it will work shows as "?" until Listen has revealed the temperament: Watch gives where and when, Listen gives who they are. Finding out is what turns a gamble into a plan.

Who knows what Spec

A person knows a fact only if they saw it (a clear sightline within 13 m) or were told it by someone they are tied to: face to face within 20 m, or by phone to someone indoors, since calls are voice. A told fact is never passed on again. At the start nobody knows anything about the cell, and the cell is known by face only, never by name. A shop or café keeper knows the needs of their workmates and regulars, which is why the café owner's tips are worth having. Facts travel along ties, never opinion; the one feeling that travels is the word of someone the cell helped or harmed, between missions (below). Investigators question the people the simulation tracks in detail; the background crowd adds Trail, Alert and standing but cannot be questioned.

Standing: heroes or menace

Each district rates you on a Hero ↔ Menace scale: Hero from +3, Menace from −3. Every district starts at +2, leaning Hero: "Hero is kinda the default, if you're not seen then everyone assumes you're good (it's that kinda world)" (Sky). One known kindness earns the band. Spec

  • In a mission, only acts seen or found move it. Each seen threat, act of violence, drawn weapon, takedown or carry is −1. A killing that is found is −1 even if nobody saw it. A missing person moves nothing.
  • A public fight counts once, by who you fought. A fight is public if city people are within 30 m of any shot; it moves Standing once, when it ends. Firing on the guard, the patrol, officers or robots is −1. Firing first on rivals the district doesn't fear is −1. Breaking rivals the district fears is +1 ("a rival gang that has menace level authority is a +1", Sky). Anything else is 0. How the public sees a mission's rivals is part of the mission; the Handover's rivals are feared.
  • Word of mouth, between missions. "If you help in a good way then can move to hero" (Sky). Each person you helped tells their family and workmates (+1); each one you pressured or knocked out tells of the harm (−1). It counts once per person, a person both helped and harmed counts as harmed, and the word moves a district at most 2 a mission. It is a feeling, not a fact: no face, no place, nothing an investigator can use.
  • The city forgives. A district where nothing moved Standing drifts one step back toward +2, from either side, so Hero has to be kept too.

Helping people, shielding civilians, driving off feared rivals in public and freeing arrested locals push toward Hero. Shooting in crowds, public threats, harm to bystanders, fighting the police and a killing found push toward Menace. An unseen threat moves Standing only through the victim's word. Neither end loses. They are two ways to control the city:

HeroMenace
Turning peopleSlower and dearer, loyal resultsFaster and cheaper, with betrayal risk
CrowdsJoin your fights and hide your operativesObey out of fear, report when they can, scatter under fire
FightsFewer, and police hesitate in crowdsMore often, and police and rivals come in harder
The street shows itHero graffiti, cheering, free tipsWanted posters, averted eyes, empty pavements
05 · PRESSURE

The city moves without you

Urgency comes from scheduled events with a reason behind them, never from an arbitrary countdown. Each mission defines its own closing event.

Security

  • A guard on a door routine, with a café stop before his shift.
  • Every staff post checks in by voice every 90 s from the start of its shift, and at its end. A missed check-in is a report, and the Scout can learn the marks. Spec
  • Surveillance with fixed cones, blocked by roofs and parked vehicles, on a screen a person scans every 20 s. You see a cone only once the Scout has watched it; a watcher you haven't watched shows "?", and it still sees you. Spec
  • A patrol on a sweep, which breaks off toward gunfire within 30 m.
  • The response comes by the dial below. The district seals the level's seal time (2:25 at the Handover) after an incident is confirmed at Alert 2 or more and the response is on the street. Built

Rivals

  • A rival crew after the same target, on its own schedule. Their Handover schedule is in §07.
  • A false tip sends them away for 3:50. Gunfire brings them within 16 s. Built

Alert, 0 to 3

LevelSecurity doesRaised by
0 · RoutineFollows its schedules—
1 · InquiryRobots check the reported spot. The patrol tightens its sweep.A report that lands of a found knockout, a woken victim, a noise, a missed check-in or a missing person; a discovered fault; counted once per incident Spec
2 · SearchSends the response unit and robots to the place; their search opens hiding places within 30 mA second incident; a report that lands of a found kill or a carry seen; any gunfire at once (§06), which sets Alert to at least 2; a shot no longer adds +1 each Built
3 · LockdownExterior doors lock (security level 2 and up), units cordon the district's mouths, and the district begins to seal.A report that lands of a takedown seen; gunfire or violence seen by a civilian sets 3 at once Built

Silent acts wait for the report. A takedown, a carry, a body or a missing person raises Alert only when someone's report reaches security, never at the moment it is seen; gunfire raises it at once, because security hears it. Witness Trail and Standing still move at sight. A knockout that is found, or wakes and reports, never raises Alert above 1; a takedown seen is 3 when it is reported, knockout or not. One takedown is one incident and one dispatch, however many people find it. Spec

The crowd is cover and witness Spec

Anyone with a clear line of sight within 13 m of a traceable act becomes a witness, adding +1 Trail per incident and moving Standing. Dense crowds also break the sightlines of guards and cameras. Busy streets are both a hiding place and a risk. Turning is private (§04): asking, paying, helping and listening have no witnesses. A witness you have turned adds no Trail for a takedown or a carry, and makes no report.

Running is noticed Spec. A runner is noticed wherever an act would be: by people with a clear line within 13 m, and in the cones of the guard, the patrol, live cameras, the response unit and the rivals. People remember where and when they saw the runner, and the Fixer's face if it was him: a lead for investigators, but no Trail and no change in standing. Security that sees a runner counts it a fault and checks it: Alert rises to at least 1, once per run, and a guard who saw you run no longer fights at your side. Once a fight is on, the run is loud or you are under fire, running is free.

A drawn weapon is an act Spec. Seen by security, it raises Alert to at least 2 and that watcher engages: two seconds, then it fires. Seen by people within 13 m, it is one witnessed incident (+1 Trail, Alert at least 1), and they remember the face. A weapon drawn where nobody sees it costs nothing.

Alarm inside Spec. Once Alert reaches 2, the target's building hides them: entering takes 30 s longer (in the Handover, 68 s instead of 38).

Levels Spec. Sightlines and the 13 m run in three dimensions: a deck blocks sight straight up and down, an open edge does not. People change level only by stair, ramp, escalator or lift, and that takes time. Watchers stand on every level; a station's watcher covers its concourse. A crowded deck above a quiet service lane is a choice the player can see.

The news travels on foot Spec

With no networks, a fact reaches security only through a person. Whoever notices a takedown, a carry or a body reacts by who they are. Staff radio it from where they stand (5 s). The victim's lover or family report at once. Someone the cell has turned keeps quiet, and a person turned for this very act (the driver who brought the car) is never its witness. An Informer reports; a terrified person flees and never reports. Then by temperament: the Loyal report, Idealists walk over to check the body and then report, Mercenaries keep quiet until Alert 2, and the Fearful flee or avoid it and tell someone instead.

A reporter walks, or runs after an act, to the nearest place with a phone: a staffed door or a street call box (the world places them so every street point is within 40 m of one), and calls (6 s). Only then does the report land. A live camera's lands at its next scan, a robot's in 4 s. That walk is the player's window, and it is on screen: a "!" over the witness and a dotted line to the phone. Take the reporter down before the call ends and the report is dropped. Whoever saw something also tells one person: face to face within 20 m, or by phone to someone indoors. The Tech can't cut a call box.

Bodies stay where they fall Spec

"Civilians can see bodies. They don't disappear; the enforcer has to take them into a quiet place" (Sky). Someone knocked out or killed lies where they fell until moved, and kills are shown, not cut away. Anyone within 13 m with a clear line finds an open body, and so does any watcher whose cone covers it. Only a hiding place hides one: a large bin or crate (5 s, in the street, so it is seen as a carry; it holds one) or a service door (10 s, off screen; it holds three). Bins are emptied on a round every 15 minutes, and the Scout can learn when.

Someone knocked out wakes after 2:00, staggers, and reports the assault (Alert 1, and what they know becomes leads). Hidden, they call out every 10 s, heard within 20 m; tied up, they are silent until someone frees them. A found knockout lands at Alert 1, a found kill at 2, a carry seen at 2 and a takedown seen at 3. A found body holds the scene: officers come at any Alert, and the door the body lies at and every door within 13 m in sight of it refuse entry and exit until they stand down (1:00 at Alert 1, 3:00 at Alert 2, never at Alert 3). A body moved before the officers arrive makes the report unfounded. At Alert 2 or more their search opens every hiding place within 30 m. Preparation earns the right to leave a body: with the camera looped and the patrol rerouted, nobody may come in time.

A missing person is noticed Spec

Someone due to meet a lover, a relative or a workmate at a place they share, who finds them gone, raises the alarm after 20 s (Alert 1). The expectations come from people's routines; none is written by hand. A turned waiter says nothing, and a person being taken can't report anything.

The response is a dial Spec

"It's easy to swarm the play area with robots if we need to temper the game play" (Sky). How hard a district answers is data per district and mission, not code: the security level is the district's base, plus one for every two open cases (at most two), plus the mission's own bonus. The Handover runs at level 2.
