  "schema": "suborned.routines.rules/1",
  "author": "Pulse (brief 022, 2026-10-18)",
  "gdd": "the-suborned-agent-gdd-v0.23.0-2026-10-17.md",
  "status": "proposed: Keel's engine does not read this file yet. Nothing here moves a recorded run; the numbers join the rulebook (contracts/rules/rulebook.json, Motive confirms) when Keel lands the reader.",
  "rule": "How a person works their post, and what two partners do when they meet (Sky 2026-10-18, after playing the Handover with real figures: \"have the waitress also walk around the cafe tables, and when guard comes, they stand together\"). A stop in the people file says where a person is based; a round says how they work it. Both rules are about people, not about Inez: the generator (tools/routines/rounds.ts) finds the people they apply to from their job, their stop and their ties, and nothing here names a person. Same inputs, same bytes. Tags: [B] built, [S] starting value to tune by playtest; `of` names the rulebook value a number copies, and tools/routines/rounds.test.ts holds them equal.",
  "rounds": {
    "who": {
      "jobs": ["server"],
      "stop": "a stop out on the street at a unit's door (post: door) whose unit has a terrace of tables",
      "terraces": { "cafe-entrance": "cafe-table-" },
      "src": "Sky 2026-10-18 (the waitress walks the tables); briefs/014/pulse-cafe.md (a door is one person's post, so one server is drawn at the café door and she is the one who works the terrace)",
      "reason": "keyed by job and stop, never by id: any server who stands a door with tables beside it works them, in any café the plan draws. A server who works inside is not drawn, so she has no round."
    },
    "pace": { "cmPerS": 140, "of": "values.op-speed-cm-s", "src": "life.json pedestrians.walkSpeed 1.4 m/s; rulebook op-speed-cm-s [S]", "reason": "the world's one walking pace, so Latch plays the one walk clip and a leg's seconds are its length over 1.4 m/s, rounded up to a whole second (never faster than the cell)." },
    "opening": {
      "settleS": 30,
      "src": "briefs/022-living-cafe.md consequences; GDD §07 schedule: 0:00 routines run, the camera opens on the cell",
      "proposed": true,
      "reason": "no excursion starts before 0:30, so what the player sees first is Inez at her door; the Scout's Watch (20 s) and his first Listen reach her where the briefing put her. Readable before rich."
    },
    "rest": {
      "s": [24, 36],
      "src": "briefs/022-living-cafe.md; Pulse numbers [S]",
      "proposed": true,
      "reason": "she stands her post between excursions. At 24 to 36 s she is at the door about half the time (a window the player sees coming) and back every minute or so; shorter and she is never there to be turned, longer and she is not walking round the tables."
    },
    "serve": {
      "s": [12, 18],
      "src": "briefs/022-living-cafe.md; Pulse numbers [S]",
      "proposed": true,
      "reason": "the pause at a table: long enough to read as taking an order (Latch's talk clip), short enough that a table 19 m away still brings her back inside a minute."
    },
    "demand": {
      "greetS": 10,
      "revisitS": [75, 105],
      "src": "briefs/022-living-cafe.md; Pulse numbers [S]",
      "proposed": true,
      "reason": "she goes where people sit: a new party is greeted greetS after it sits, a seated table is visited again every revisitS, the most overdue first (then the nearer, then the lower table). A table already seated at 0:00 is due at a seeded moment between settleS and the longest revisit, so the first minute is not a queue. An empty table is never visited. Occupancy is read from the people file's seat stops of drawn walkers; the four cast roles are not counted, because the engine plays them by their role, not by their routine."
    },
    "servicePoint": {
      "ringCm": [130, 110, 150, 170],
      "clearOfSeatCm": 60,
      "face": "the table",
      "src": "briefs/022-living-cafe.md; tools/decokit/furnish_cafe.py (three chairs at 72 cm round a table, 120 degrees apart)",
      "proposed": true,
      "reason": "she stands in the gap between two chairs, on the first ring that is free ground on the site's walk grid, the gap the shortest walk from her post reaches. 60 cm from every chair keeps her off a customer (P-16, no two on one place)."
    },
    "leashM": { "v": 25, "src": "briefs/022-living-cafe.md", "proposed": true, "reason": "a table further than 25 m of walking from her post is not hers; the flank tables are 15 to 19 m, so all eight tables are." },
    "horizonS": { "v": 900, "src": "mission window 8 to 12 min (GDD §01)", "reason": "the round is baked for 15 minutes of round clock, which holds cover the longest mission (12 min) with room; after it she stands her post." },
    "clock": {
      "rule": "the round runs on a round clock that starts at 0 at the mission's first second (or at the stop's start, if it begins later) and stops while she is held. The baked excursions are on that clock.",
      "src": "briefs/022-living-cafe.md",
      "reason": "one primitive for every interruption: stop the clock, put her somewhere, start it again. Nothing is rebuilt and nothing replays differently."
    },
    "holds": {
      "verbs": ["listen", "ask", "pay", "help", "pressure"],
      "from": "the tick the order is taken",
      "until": "the tick it lands, plus lingerS",
      "lingerS": 3,
      "where": "stands where she is, turned toward the operative",
      "src": "GDD §04 turning is a conversation; briefs/022-living-cafe.md",
      "proposed": true,
      "reason": "a person being spoken to stands still: reach is checked when the order is given, so she must not walk off from under it. lingerS lets a recorded chain re-issue at the tick the last order lands (Help, then Help, then the call, as route A does). Watch holds nothing: the Scout watching her is how he learns the round."
    },
    "ends": {
      "on": ["alert-2", "gunfire", "body-found", "final-fight"],
      "then": "she walks the way she came to her post (a leg's own seconds, never more than the longest leg) and stands it for the rest of the mission",
      "src": "GDD §05 crowds within 30 m of gunfire scatter; the café door is her refuge; briefs/022-living-cafe.md",
      "proposed": true,
      "reason": "the loud and the fighting parts of every mission are played with Inez at her door, as they were recorded: nothing in the fights, the response or the cover reads a moving Inez. Quiet play is where her round runs."
    },
    "called": {
      "when": "the Fixer's call is taken and her lover will come",
      "does": "she breaks off, walks the way she came to her post, and the round clock stops until the visit is over",
      "resumes": "partS after he turns to go, at the start of the next rest",
      "src": "GDD §07 the capstone; rulebook summon; briefs/022-living-cafe.md",
      "reason": "the visit is always at her post, so its walk, window and sightlines are the ones the Handover was built on."
    }
  },
  "partners": {
    "kinds": ["lover"],
    "closeCm": { "v": 120, "src": "briefs/022-living-cafe.md; Sky 2026-10-18 (they stand together)", "proposed": true, "reason": "arm's length: far enough that two bodies (65 cm clearance on the walk grid) never overlap, near enough to read as a couple. Well inside together-m (4 m), so a Watch that ends with them standing together still teaches the affair." },
    "partS": { "v": 2, "src": "briefs/022-living-cafe.md", "proposed": true, "reason": "the beat they stand turned to each other before the one who came turns away." },
    "clearCm": { "v": 100, "src": "briefs/022-living-cafe.md addendum (Sky 2026-10-18: \"the guard stops on top of the Scout\"); the walk grid's 65 cm body clearance", "proposed": true, "reason": "the summoned partner never stops within a metre of anyone else: two bodies and a hand's width. Read at the tick of the call, over the operatives and everyone on the street." },
    "summoned": {
      "meetAt": "the post of the one who called",
      "stay": { "s": 60, "of": "values.lover-stay-s" },
      "face": "each other",
      "side": {
        "stepDeg": 15,
        "order": "angle off her facing nearest 90 degrees first (a side, then the front quarter), then her left (east of a south-facing post) before her right; free ground only",
        "pick": "the first stop with nobody within clearCm of it; if every stop is taken, the stop whose nearest person is farthest, the earlier in the list on a tie; if the file has no stop, the old stop: on his own route, closeCm short of her post",
        "src": "briefs/022-living-cafe.md addendum (Pulse; Waymark's c020 play note: the guard stops 0.9 m from the Scout at beside-inez)",
        "proposed": true,
        "reason": "a couple stand side by side, not one behind the other on the line the cell walks up. Her post is a door alcove 2 m wide: at closeCm only the front quarter (up to 45 degrees off her facing, either hand) is free ground, so that is where he stands, 1.5 m from the Listen point instead of 0.9 m. The stops are made at build time from the walk grid; the engine only picks, so there is no trigonometry and no float at runtime."
      },
      "src": "GDD §07 route A (the guard walks over, stays, returns); rulebook summon; Sky 2026-10-18",
      "proposed": true,
      "reason": "he walks the route he always walked to her post and stops closeCm from it, at her side (side), and faces her; she faces him. Walk and window follow the world: his stop is the grid's, never a number written here."
    },
    "chance": {
      "noticeM": 8,
      "stayS": 20,
      "perPair": 1,
      "who": "two walkers whose ties include a partner kind, both out on the street, neither held, neither on a post, the first time in the mission their routines bring them within noticeM on a clear line",
      "shape": "an excursion for each: leave the routine point, walk to their place beside the other, stand facing, walk back, and the routine clock stops for it",
      "src": "Sky 2026-10-18 (\"meets her off shift\"); briefs/022-living-cafe.md",
      "proposed": true,
      "reason": "two partners do not pass each other: they stop for stayS. It happens once a mission for a pair, so a couple on the same street all day is not a queue. A person on a post is not a walker: the guard is met at his door only by the summons. The Harbour cast has two lover pairs and no chance meeting in the mission window; the rule is for the missions the generator makes."
    }
  }
}

contracts/rules/rulebook.json.text:
{
 "schema": "suborned.rulebook/1",
 "author": "Keel (brief 010, 2026-10-15)",
 "gdd": "the-suborned-agent-gdd-v0.22.0-2026-10-15.md",
 "rule": "Every event the city simulation runs: what it needs, what it charges, what it changes and who sees it (GDD §11: events carry conditions, effects, witnesses). Anything not in this file or in people.rules.json is rejected (§01: unknown = reject). Scales, temperaments, needs, ties, the Talker test, knowledge and the reference approach prices are read from people.rules.json through p: refs and condition kinds, never restated here. Every number lives once in `values`, tagged as the GDD tags it: [B] built and proven in the top-down test, [S] starting value to tune by playtest, [L] later; a value or rule the GDD does not decide carries proposed: true and a reason, for Sky. Conditions are keyed by `k`, effects by `do`, always the first key, so the C# engine reads them as tagged unions. Outcomes are tried in order and the first whose conditions all hold applies; the last has none, so every event resolves to exactly one outcome. `also` entries apply after the outcome, in order.",
 "reads": {
  "people": {
   "path": "contracts/people/people.rules.json",
   "schema": "suborned.people.rules/1",
   "reads": [
    "scales: min, max and named steps; every move clamps to them",
    "temperaments: respondsTo, refuses and reportsApproach decide an approach's fit; start values",
    "approaches: requires, usd, timeS and trail are the base price line of each Turn event",
    "needs.list: metBy (which approach acts on a need), requires (what a replacement need may need)",
    "ties.kinds: introduces (K5) and between (K4)",
    "talker: test, facts and lie",
    "knowledge: needsKnown positions (K9), identity face only, learnedBy witnessed or told",
    "tiers: only the simulated carry memory and can be questioned (Sky Q5)"
   ]
  }
 },
 "tags": {
  "B": "built: proven in the top-down test (~/Projects/the-suborned/testbed/reference/suborned-world-sim.cjs) or stated [B] in the GDD",
  "S": "spec: a starting value the GDD states [S], tuned by playtest",
  "L": "later: after the capstone"
 },
 "units": {
  "usd": "integer dollars",
  "s": "integer seconds; the engine steps at 10 Hz (§11), so 1 s = 10 ticks",
  "m": "metres, compared in 3D (§05 levels)",
  "trail": "Trail points, integer, campaign scope",
  "alert": "Alert level, integer 0–3, mission scope",
  "standing": "district standing, integer: above 0 Hero, below 0 Menace",
  "orders": "orders of the same approach to the same person",
  "scale-steps": "steps on a people.rules.json scale",
  "ticks": "engine ticks, 10 a second",
  "entries": "memory entries",
  "hops": "ties crossed by one piece of news",
  "count": "a plain count",
  "cm": "centimetres",
  "cm-per-s": "centimetres a second",
  "per-mille": "integer weight scale for seeded draws",
  "pct": "integer per cent"
 },
 "values": {
  "watch-s": { "v": 20, "unit": "s", "tag": "S", "src": "Sky 2026-10-15 (Motive's balance, briefs/011/motive-balance.md): Watch 20 s; §04 Pay requires routine known (Watch); the top-down test's watchCafe was 52 s [B]", "proposed": true, "reason": "Motive balance (brief 011, Suture E-8, T2): at 52 s the informed route A calls at 2:42 and loud (3:38) beats it. At 20 s the call is at 2:10, inside the 2:13-2:47 sweep gap, and route A finishes at 3:33, 5 s before the best loud. Watch keeps its place in the chain (Watch, then Listen, then Help) and Sky's Pay lesson stays on the main path: after Watch the Pay card shows '?' and $90,000 worst case. Sky's steer to more real-time also argues for shorter prep timers." },
  "watch-sight-reach-m": { "v": 18, "unit": "m", "tag": "S", "src": "Sky 2026-10-16: view cones are the Scout's skill (Glyph, briefs/011/ui/review-2026-10-16 §3.4: a watcher within 18 m on a clear line)", "proposed": true, "reason": "the GDD gives no reach for watching a watcher. A camera or a patrol is watched from across the street, not from beside it as a person is (act-reach-m 6 m): 18 m is a walking guard's sight (facing-reach-m), so the Scout can watch from outside most cones but not from anywhere." },
  "watch-routine-s": { "v": 40, "unit": "s", "tag": "S", "src": "Sky 2026-10-16: a timed Watch also teaches the watcher's routine (stage 2; Aster's brief to Keel)", "proposed": true, "reason": "the GDD gives no time. Two Watches (2 × watch-s) of a watcher with a cycle (the patrol's sweep) teach when it turns and when it sees the door: the price of a timing plan is Scout time, set against Reroute (45 s and 1 Trail) that it can replace. Motive prices it." },
  "listen-s": { "v": 42, "unit": "s", "tag": "B", "src": "§04 Help requires need known (Listen 42 s); top-down test listenInez" },
  "listen-reach-m": { "v": 3, "unit": "m", "tag": "B", "src": "top-down test listenInez reach 3" },
  "approach-reach-m": { "v": 4, "unit": "m", "tag": "B", "src": "top-down test askInez, offerInez, turnInez, pressureInez reach 4" },
  "refusal-usd": { "v": 10000, "unit": "usd", "tag": "B", "src": "§04 Ask cold leaves a remembered refusal: later offers +$10,000; top-down test offerInez, turnInez (+$10,000 when inezRefused)" },
  "refusal-trail": { "v": 1, "unit": "trail", "tag": "B", "src": "§04 remembered refusal: +1 T; top-down test offerInez, turnInez, pressureInez (+1 T when inezRefused; pressure adds no $)" },
  "help-orders": { "v": 1, "unit": "orders", "tag": "B", "src": "§07 route A: Fixer helps Inez ($40,000), once" },
  "worse-help-orders": { "v": 1, "unit": "orders", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 wrong approach [S] (Sky Q4): one more Help; §04 Fearful, Hero: needs Help ×2" },
  "worse-pay-usd": { "v": 20000, "unit": "usd", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 wrong approach [S] (Sky Q4): a higher price, Keel sets the number", "proposed": true, "reason": "Pay's step is money. $20,000 is twice the refusal surcharge, so a wrong approach costs more than a cold ask's leftover, and it keeps every §04 lesson: a Mercenary is cheapest by Pay ($70,000 < Help ×2 $80,000), a Fearful or Loyal person is cheaper by Help ($80,000 < $90,000) but slower (100 s vs 50 s), and Pay plus the driver stays over the purse." },
  "worse-pressure-trail": { "v": 1, "unit": "trail", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 wrong approach [S] (Sky Q4): a higher price; Pressure's price is Trail", "proposed": true, "reason": "Pressure costs no money, so its step is +1 T (a louder threat), in one order. A second threat instead would add a second +1 resentment and make an Informer of anyone not Fearful (resentment max 2): a cliff, not a step." },
  "loyal-help-orders": { "v": 1, "unit": "orders", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 Loyal (institution): trust over time; Hero: turns after repeated Help", "proposed": true, "reason": "'repeated' read as the smallest repeat: one Help more than anyone else, so a Loyal person turns on the second Help even though Help suits them." },
  "mercenary-hero-usd": { "v": 20000, "unit": "usd", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 Mercenary, Hero: overcharges; Motive K8 (CK3 additive line items)", "proposed": true, "reason": "the same size as the wrong-approach step, so the preview's lines read in one currency of steps: a Hero district's Mercenary costs what a wrong Pay costs." },
  "mercenary-menace-usd": { "v": -20000, "unit": "usd", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 Mercenary, Menace: discount", "proposed": true, "reason": "the mirror of the Hero overcharge: one step off ($50,000 for Inez's reference Pay)." },
  "standing-start": { "v": 2, "unit": "standing", "tag": "S", "src": "Sky 2026-10-16 ('Hero is kinda the default, if you're not seen then everyone assumes you're good (it's that kinda world)'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md rule 1 (approved by Sky, 'sure', 2026-10-16); was 0", "proposed": true, "reason": "Motive: every district starts leaning Hero, one step short of the Hero band, so one known kindness earns the band. Starting at +3 would put the Handover in Hero prices from the first second and change its tested costs; at +2 every in-mission price stays neutral." },
  "standing-step": { "v": 1, "unit": "standing", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 standing: witnessed acts only; §05 witness moves standing", "proposed": true, "reason": "one step per witnessed incident, as Trail counts one point per incident: one incident counts once." },
  "hero-at": { "v": 3, "unit": "standing", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 standing table (turning, crowds, fights, street change at each end)", "proposed": true, "reason": "the Hero and Menace columns need a threshold. Three witnessed incidents one way make a district Hero (or Menace at −3): a mission or two of deliberate play, so the player sees it coming and chooses it." },
  "menace-at": { "v": -3, "unit": "standing", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 standing table", "proposed": true, "reason": "as hero-at, mirrored." },
  "word-standing-step": { "v": 1, "unit": "standing", "tag": "S", "src": "Sky 2026-10-16 ('if you help in a good way then can move to hero'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md rules 2 and 3", "proposed": true, "reason": "Motive: between missions each person the cell helped tells their ties a stranger helped them (+1), and each person it pressured or knocked out tells of the harm (−1): one step per person, not per tie, so a large family is no lever." },
  "word-standing-cap": { "v": 2, "unit": "standing", "tag": "S", "src": "Sky 2026-10-16 ('if you help in a good way then can move to hero'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md rules 2 and 3", "proposed": true, "reason": "Motive: the word moves a district at most 2 steps either way in one mission, so turning a crowd of kind strangers cannot buy the Hero band outright and a bad mission's word cannot sink a district alone; seen and found acts stay uncapped." },
  "standing-drift": { "v": 1, "unit": "standing", "tag": "S", "src": "Sky 2026-10-16 (approved Motive's 'the benefit of the doubt'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md rule 5", "proposed": true, "reason": "Motive: what the city stops seeing, it forgives. A district where nothing moved Standing this mission moves 1 step back toward standing-start, from either side, never past it: unkept Hero fades back to +2 as Menace does, so Hero is kept by doing good and a Menace cell is not stuck." },
  "fight-standing-step": { "v": 1, "unit": "standing", "tag": "S", "src": "Sky 2026-10-16 (via Aster: 'it should be per fight, and depends who you're fighting - a rival gang that has menace level authority is a +1'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md, a public fight, rule 3", "proposed": true, "reason": "Motive: the public judges a fight by its enemy, once per fight: one step, toward Menace for a fight with authority or for firing first on rivals nobody fears, toward Hero for driving off a crew the district fears." },
  "witness-range-m": { "v": 13, "unit": "m", "tag": "S", "src": "§05 witness [S]: clear sightline within 13 m; §05 levels: in 3D; top-down test inezWitness ≤ 13" },
  "witness-trail": { "v": 1, "unit": "trail", "tag": "S", "src": "§05 witness [S]: +1 T per incident" },
  "alert-inquiry": { "v": 1, "unit": "alert", "tag": "S", "src": "§05 Alert 1 inquiry [S]: witness report or found fault, once per incident" },
  "alert-search": { "v": 2, "unit": "alert", "tag": "B", "src": "§05 Alert 2 search [B]: 2nd incident or any gunfire" },
  "alert-lockdown": { "v": 3, "unit": "alert", "tag": "B", "src": "§05 Alert 3 lockdown [B]: violence seen by a civilian → 3 at once" },
  "trail-open": { "v": 1, "unit": "trail", "tag": "S", "src": "§05 watchers: once a Trail is open, investigators can pull the log; §08 investigation little at T 0" },
  "bravery-per-job": { "v": 1, "unit": "scale-steps", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 bravery [S]: +1 step per job completed unexposed" },
  "resentment-per-exposure": { "v": 1, "unit": "scale-steps", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 resentment [S]: +1 step per pressure or exposure" },
  "resentment-per-pressure": { "v": 1, "unit": "scale-steps", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 resentment [S]: +1 step per pressure or exposure" },
  "fear-per-pressure": { "v": 1, "unit": "scale-steps", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 Pressure leaves fear; §05 a threat adds fear; people.rules scales.fear (one step per pressure or threat)" },
  "loyalty-per-help": { "v": 1, "unit": "scale-steps", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 Help leaves gratitude; people.rules scales.loyalty: only being turned raises it", "proposed": true, "reason": "gratitude made a number: each Help that lands is +1 loyalty to the cell (obliged, then trusting). It is what quiets a helped contact under questioning (Talker test) and what keeps a Fearful person from talking once helped (people.rules temperaments.fearful)." },
  "loyalty-per-volunteer": { "v": 1, "unit": "scale-steps", "tag": "S", "src": "§04 Idealist, Hero: volunteers free; standing table: Hero turning is loyal", "proposed": true, "reason": "an Idealist who volunteers in a Hero district starts obliged, as a helped one does." },
  "violence-bravery": { "v": -1, "unit": "scale-steps", "tag": "S", "src": "§06 civilians targetable: a contact who witnesses loses bravery, gains fear and resentment", "proposed": true, "reason": "one step each way, the size of every other ladder move." },
  "violence-fear": { "v": 1, "unit": "scale-steps", "tag": "S", "src": "§06 civilians targetable", "proposed": true, "reason": "as violence-bravery." },
  "violence-resentment": { "v": 1, "unit": "scale-steps", "tag": "S", "src": "§06 civilians targetable", "proposed": true, "reason": "as violence-bravery." },
  "memory-cap": { "v": 8, "unit": "entries", "tag": "S", "src": "Motive K1: capped per person [S]; DF holds 8 short-term memories (dwarf-fortress.md §3)", "proposed": true, "reason": "eight entries hold a person's whole part in a district's campaign (an approach, a job or two, what they saw, what they were told). When full the oldest goes: an old sighting is forgotten, which is the GDD's 'sightings go stale' (§05 counters) made a rule. Fixed size suits the engine's integer arrays." },
  "word-hops": { "v": 1, "unit": "hops", "tag": "S", "src": "Motive K3: word passes along ties between missions, one hop; §04 knowledge [S] (Sky Q6): news travels along ties as facts", "proposed": true, "reason": "the GDD says news travels along ties; how far is not stated. One hop, between missions only, keeps the spread countable in the debrief." },
  "word-quiet-loyalty": { "v": 1, "unit": "scale-steps", "tag": "S", "src": "§01 pillar subvert people: does knowing more make a person quieter?; Motive's review #10 (briefs/010/motive-rulebook-review.md)", "proposed": true, "reason": "a person who owes the cell (obliged or more) keeps what they saw to themselves; one Help, which needs a Listen, is enough; at 2 a helped Inez would lie to investigators and still tell her family the Fixer's face. Obliged is also the line for reporting and selling." },
  "introductions-per-contact": { "v": 1, "unit": "count", "tag": "S", "src": "Motive K5: one introduction per contact between missions [S]; §04 between missions: introduces a friend" },
  "question-s": { "v": 20, "unit": "s", "tag": "S", "src": "§05 investigators [S]: on foot question ~every 20 s" },
  "hop-min-s": { "v": 60, "unit": "s", "tag": "S", "src": "§05 investigators: ~60–90 s per hop" },
  "hop-max-s": { "v": 90, "unit": "s", "tag": "S", "src": "§05 investigators: ~60–90 s per hop" },
  "need-weight-scale": { "v": 1000, "unit": "per-mille", "tag": "S", "src": "§11 integer state; §04 needs (Sky Q2) replacement drawn from the person's own stream", "proposed": true, "reason": "the cast rows weight needs as decimals (cast.schema.ts, ≤ 100). The engine draws in integers only, so the export scales each weight by 1,000 and rounds; the same integers in C# and TS give the same draw." },
  "op-speed-cm-s": { "v": 140, "unit": "cm-per-s", "tag": "S", "src": "life.json pedestrians.walkSpeed 1.4 m/s [S]", "proposed": true, "reason": "the operatives walk at the world's one walking pace. The top-down test moved them 1.1 units/s on an unscaled map; the real civic block is in metres, and a second pace would make the cell read as faster than the city." },
  "op-run-speed-cm-s": { "v": 280, "unit": "cm-per-s", "tag": "S", "src": "Sky 2026-10-15, briefs/011/motive-fights.md: run at 2.8 m/s (Q2); Syndicate Wars double-click run", "proposed": true, "reason": "2× the walk, so the chip reads half the time. Faster than the response unit's 2.2 m/s [B], and that's fine: the police's threat is cones, guns and the seal, never a foot race." },
  "act-reach-m": { "v": 6, "unit": "m", "tag": "B", "src": "the top-down test (~/Projects/the-suborned/testbed/reference/suborned-world-sim.cjs, sha256 0b3a7add…): an action's default reach (nearby: reach || 6)" },
  "loop-s": { "v": 62, "unit": "s", "tag": "B", "src": "§07 route A: Tech loops entrance camera (1:02, tethered); top-down test loopCamera" },

  "rule": "A cancel order stops what one operative is doing now, the activity the HUD shows: an act in progress first, then a walk or run, then a fire order, then a draw, then a loop held, then a downed operative carried. Each verb's line says what cancelling it costs or keeps. stop: the operative stands where they are. holster: a draw not yet done goes back. cease: the fire order ends, the weapon stays drawn. lost: the act's time is spent and nothing lands (Watch and Listen learn nothing; a Loop, Reroute, Mislead or lift not finished does nothing; their Trail is charged only when they land). aborted: the approach stops mid-conversation; the money held for it comes back (the engine holds the price at the order and pays it only in the outcome's charge, Redline E2), no Trail, and the person remembers an aborted approach (memory act `aborted`, with the Fixer's face): it is no refusal, so the approach may be tried again, but it is a fact an investigator can get. ends: the loop stops and the camera comes back. staff-report: the Enforcer comes back out without Vale by the public door, or by the service door if a unit holds the public door, or waits inside while both are held (response; brief 013 E3); the Office staff report the intruder, one reported incident (alert.byIncident). vale-reports: Vale is let go at his car and reports the attempt, one reported incident, and he remembers the aborted take (memory act `aborted`, the Enforcer's face), so an investigator who questions him finds a lead (Motive addendum Q4). put-down: the carried operative is laid down where the carrier stands. Go is instant and has nothing to cancel; a Board or a step-out cancelled spends the time and lands nothing (lost). Putting Vale down is no cancel: the Enforcer keeps him (a rule of its own if Sky wants one). The verbs whose line may change take one of: turn aborted or lost; enter staff-report or quiet; take vale-reports or quiet. Brief 013: a takedown cancelled before it lands lets the victim go (`takedown` released): he saw the Enforcer and reports it as a woken victim would; lifting, dropping, stashing or tying a body cancelled spends the time and lands nothing (`body` lost); a body carried is laid down where the carrier stands (`carrying` put-down).",

  "src": "Sky 2026-10-15 playtest: \"there's nothing showing me what the cell player is doing when they're busy, nor is there a way to cancel their action\" (Aster)",

Keel's proposal: cancelling an act already under way spends its time and lands nothing, as a refusal does; the money held comes back because it was never handed over; the two acts that put a stranger in front of someone (Enter, Take) leave a report, as an interrupted intrusion would; a broken-off approach leaves the person the Fixer's face but no refusal, so cancel is no free retry of a bad card but no punishment like a refusal either."

  "rule": "The Enforcer's takedown (brief 013, Sky 2026-10-16: anyone can be targeted; one rule set for every simulated person, no named target list). The Enforcer alone, standing within `reach` of a person on the street, knocks them out (`ko`) or kills them (`kill`); silent: none of the gunfire rules apply, no money. Vale may be killed (the mission fails, §07) but not knocked out (use Take); the patrol and cameras are no targets (Reroute and Loop are their verbs). A target who had the Enforcer in his cone when the order was given, heard him running within witness range, or witnessed one of the cell's acts this mission (a takedown, a carry, a drawn weapon: Motive rev 3, until a stop has a facing) is aware: unarmed, he struggles (`struggle` more), screams (heard within witness.scream) and holds the Enforcer's face; armed (a person with a weapon: the door guard), the takedown fails, he draws and engages (Alert at least weapons.costs.drawSeenSecurity at sight). The victim lies where he fell until moved: a body. A knocked-out victim wakes after `wake`, staggers `stagger`, then reports the assault whatever his temperament (a cell contact says nothing); a dead one never wakes or talks. Any operative carries a body (cell.carry lift, then walk only: the Enforcer at cell.speed, the others at carry.untrained; no run, no fire) and puts it down in carry.drop; restrains a living one in `restrain` (no move, no call-out, still seen on open ground; a finder frees him in `free`, then he reports); stashes it, standing at the stash, into a container (`stash.container`, on the street, seen as a carry) or through a service door (`stash.door`, off-screen; a door holds `stash.doorHolds` bodies, a storeroom: rev 4 R4.3; a container what its site entry says). Only a stash hides a body (two hide levels, open and shut; Sky merged call 6). A woken, unrestrained victim in a stash calls out every `callOut`, heard within witness.scream. A container is emptied by a round every `service.period`, its phase from its id, standing `service.dwell`: a body inside is found then (in the mission only; Sky merged call 9). Every number of the takedown, the price and its forecast are on the order's card before it is given.",

  "rule": "What a person does when the city's silent violence reaches them (Pulse's decision list; Motive's numbers). Who notices: a takedown or a carry, everyone on the street within witness range on a clear line at any tick of it; an open body, the same, checked every `check.ticks` (phase from the body's id); a live camera, the guard, the patrol and the response's units in their cones; a shut body nobody. The rows, first that holds, evaluated when the person notices: staff (a job in `staff`, or the door guard): radio from where he stands, landing react + postCall (the armed guard, the patrol and the response's units seeing an act or a carry engage instead: Alert at least weapons.costs.drawSeenSecurity at sight); kin of the victim (a tie in `kin`): report at once, whatever the temperament (fear `terrifiedFear`: flee); cell (turned, or loyalty at least values.word-quiet-loyalty): quiet; an Informer (resentment at its max): report; terrified (fear at least `terrifiedFear`): flee, never report; then by temperament: Loyal reports; Idealist reports, after walking to a body to learn its state (`check`); Mercenary reports only once Alert is at least `mercenaryAlert`; Fearful flees an act or carry and avoids a body. A reporter walks the grid to the nearest report point (a staffed door: the site's door refuges; a call box), at walking pace for a body and running pace (crowd.run) for an act or a carry, and calls (`call`): the report lands at the desk; a live camera's lands at its next scan (`cameraScan`, phase from its id) + postCall; a robot's after `robot`. At most `cap` reporters of one incident are in transit; one taken down, killed or carried before his report lands drops it. Whoever quiets, avoids or flees, and every reporter, tells one tie (first kind in `tells`): a tie on the street within `tell` face to face at once; a tie indoors at a unit only from a phone (calls are voice, no networks: GDD §01; Aster 2026-10-16, brief 013 E1). A reporter who walked to a report point tells from its phone when the report lands; one who radios tells face to face only, unless he stands at a report point. A quiet or avoiding person with no tie in speaking range and a tie indoors walks to the nearest report point and calls (`call`), the same walk as a report and stopped the same way (taken down, or Vale taken, before the call: nobody is told); a fleeing one calls only if the refuge her flight ends at is a staffed door. A tell is no report: it is outside `cap` and raises no Alert. A told entry, facts only, one hop (a told person never tells it on); a told Loyal person reports it from where they are. Alert rises when a report lands, never at sight (Sky merged call 1), to `alert` by what it says: a takedown seen `seen`, a carry seen `carry`, a person lying (or a noise from a stash) `down`, a dead body (staff know, an Idealist checks) `dead`, a woken victim `woken`, a missed check-in `mark`, a missing expected person `missing`; a knockout never above takedown.koAlertMax by itself; one takedown is one incident (Alert to the highest of its landed and confirmed reports; the nth reported incident at least alert.byIncident[n-1]). Witness Trail (+values.witness-trail) and Standing (traceable takedown) move once per incident at sight; a turned witness (loyalty at least values.word-quiet-loyalty) adds no Trail, and Standing still moves (Sky merged call 5). A screaming witness (fear at least `screamFear`), kin and an aware victim are heard within `scream` with no line: hearers with a line within witness range become witnesses; the rest hold heard-alarm. A reporter volunteers place and time when questioned (investigator.question, outcome volunteers). Rev 4 (Motive R4.2; Sky 2026-10-16): before every row, an accomplice of the act (a person turned to enable this very act: for the Take and its escort, the turned driver) is never its witness, whatever the tie; `kin` is lover or family only (workmate is not kin; `close`, lover, family and workmate, is whose absence or loss a person feels: expectations, the alarm's places, grief and worry). The Take: at Vale's own car with its driver turned it happens inside the car, off-screen, with no witness window (and nothing for the pickup camera to see); any other Take reads as an act for its first cell.take.struggle s, seen as a takedown by everyone within witness range on a clear line and every watcher that sees him (a live pickup camera still fails it at the order, §07). Escorted on foot, Vale looks wrong only to his kin within witness range on a clear line, or to anyone within values.near-m on a clear line who sees the grip: a carry seen. The Take and its escort are one incident, opened at the first sighting (an unseen Take opens none); witness Trail and Standing move at sight; no assault Trail is charged (the Take keeps cell.take.trailUnturned); Vale let go by a cancel reports on the same incident if it was seen.",

  "src": "briefs/013/pulse-witnesses.md §2, §3 (Pulse, third pass, aligned to Motive rev 2); briefs/013/motive-takedowns.md §1.4, §2.3; Sky 2026-10-16 merged calls 1, 2, 4, 5",

  "rule": "The response is a dial (Sky 2026-10-16: 'it's easy to swarm the play area with robots'; merged call 3): `levels` indexed by the security level S = the district's base + its open cases (campaign) + the mission's bonus, from the mission's data; the Handover's is 2. A landed alarm (a report of a silent act, a missed check-in, a missing person; gunfire, whose report lands its security.response delay less level 1's dispatch after the shot) puts the response on the street the level's `dispatch` later: at Alert 1 `a1Robots` robots; at Alert 2 or more `a2Units` units of weapons.health.responseOfficers officers (the response unit first) and `a2Robots` robots, then one more unit every `reinforce` up to `unitCap`; Alert 3 adds `a3Units` units to the district mouths (the cordon) and, where `doorsLock`, the doors lock (no Enter). A found body holds the scene (rev 4, Motive R4.1; Sky 2026-10-16): a landed report that a person lies there (down, dead, a takedown seen), the body still there and open, or a woken victim's own report where he woke, brings a unit of officers at any Alert (not bound by robot reach; not one of the dial's counted units; at Alert 2 the response unit is it), the level's dispatch after the landing. The scene holds the entrance the body lies at (within values.near-m) and every entrance within witness range of it on a clear line: from an officer's arrival (its check and its `search.s` sweep, opening stashes only at Alert 2 or more) until the unit stands down (the timers below), a held entrance refuses Enter (`door-held`) and any exit through it; an Enter under way finishes and comes out by a door not held (the service door, else the public door), or waits inside while both are held; a cancelled Enter comes out without Vale by the public door, else the service door, or waits inside while both are held (the wait cannot be cancelled; brief 013 E3). A missed check-in is an empty post, no body: it holds nothing. Counts are kept, not repeated: a later alarm tops them up. One incident is one dispatch (brief 013 D, Aster 2026-10-16): the first landed report of an incident dispatches; a later report of it that raises the Alert tops that dispatch up to the new Alert's counts, from the destinations the first set; any other later report of it sends nothing (a unit already out may be sent on to a scene no unit covers). A robot is a patrol unit (weapons.health.patrol, a pistol, trained) walking at `robotSpeed`; the patrol robot is the first robot when it is on its sweep and answers after `robotWire`; the others and the officers start at the site's docks and posts, else at the response unit's entry; they leave one every `launchGap` ticks. Robots and units stop at `cap` combatants (§06). Destinations, in order, duplicates within witness range dropped: the scene; the missing person's post and the stands his lover, family and workmates are meant to be at now, and his car (up to `spread`); the alarm-raiser's ties likewise (up to `spread`); at Alert 3 the mouths. Robots take them in order, the nearest free robot first, ties on id, each only a place within `robotReach` of where it starts (its dock, or the patrol's place on its sweep): farther places are for officers; units go to the scene, then to the place with the fewest units. A unit within witness range of the scene with a clear line verifies: a body there is confirmed (the act's Trail, a kill's Standing, Alert to the confirmed level; the seal starts only on a confirmation at Alert 2 or more, the level's `seal` after the later of the confirmation and the response unit on the street (the seal is the unit's cordon, as for gunfire; Motive rev 3); a knocked-out victim is brought round and gives his statement); no body is unfounded (Alert stays, no seal). Arriving, a unit checks `check`, then robots hold the point (a watcher) and officers search `search.s`: at Alert 2 or more they open every stash within `search.m` of the scene, nearest first, `search.stash` each; a report from a stash itself (a noise, a round) opens that stash at any Alert. Units stand down `standDown.inquiry` after the last alarm at Alert 1 and `standDown.search` at Alert 2, never at Alert 3. The world places report points and the response's origins by rule, so that every walkable cell is within `world.report` of a report point and within `world.dock` of a dock or post (R-REPORT, R-DOCK, checked by the world's tools; the engine reads the places the world exports). Every staff post checks in by voice every `checkIn` from the start of the shift at the post and at its end: a missed mark is a report that lands at the mark at the post. A person who expects a tie at a stop they share (lover, family, workmate; from the people file's routines, never authored) and is at the place without them, while the tie's routine puts them there and the tie is down, held or stashed, raises the alarm after `suspicion.s` (times `suspicion.pm` by temperament, per mille; default a flat 20 s): a missing-person report from where they stand; a turned waiter says nothing; a person being taken reports nothing.",
  "tag": "S",
  "src": "briefs/013/motive-takedowns.md §5 (the dial, check-ins, suspicion); briefs/013/pulse-witnesses.md §11-§13 and pulse-response-profiles.json (behaviour); Sky 2026-10-16 answers 4 and 6, merged call 3; Aster 2026-10-16 (both destination tiers, flat suspicion, robot speed)",

 "car": {
  "drive": "Where a car may be (brief 023). The site carries a drive grid (sim/data/handover.site.json `drive`, the walk grid's window and cells, made by tools/sim/drive.ts): a cell is drivable when its centre lies on a carriageway (within half a plan road's width of its centreline), in a kerb bay of the civic block, or on a drive (the world's vehicle crossing from a carriageway over a dropped kerb and the pavement to a bay or yard: civic-block drives[], Splice; the Handover's one is service-drive, Apron Road to serviceBay). Pavements, forecourts, yards and squares are not drivable. Every car that moves on the street routes on drivable cells only, by the walk grid's A* (8 neighbours, no corner cutting, ties by cell index, string-pulled on drivable cells): the official car's move to block the pickup camera and back, and the turned driver's drive to the service bay (by the carriageway and the drive, never across a pavement). A car's place that lies off the drive grid stands at its nearest drivable cell within 6 m (ties: lowest cell); a place with none, or a car's place that no drive reaches from the pickup, rejects the site at load (unknown = reject). A car keeps off the kerb (brief 023, Keel with Pulse): on a carriageway its centre keeps the site's drive.lane (half the city's lane, life.json traffic.laneWidth) from the edge of the drivable ground where it can, on a drive or in a bay it keeps to the middle; the route never runs nearer an edge than its grid cells did (deterministic, sim Grid.CarRoute). Timing is car.pace's: the block move takes the schedule's blockMoveS each way, and the drive to the service bay runs at its surfaces' pace from driverLast, then waits parked in the bay. Parked in the service bay the car faces the site's car.serviceFacing (the bay's long axis, nose away from the drive it came by). The getaway car leaves the street at Go along its exit lane (getaway.exit, held to the carriageway by SX-1); the rival car parks and does not move.",

   "how": [
    "the subject is one fight. The final fight is one fight, from its first shot by or at the cell to its end (fight over: every hostile down, broken or gone) or the mission's. Outside it, a fight starts at the first shot by or at the cell and ends `quiet` after the last such shot (the crowd's own 'it's over', crowd.quiet). Gunfire still open (its last shot less than `quiet` before) when the final fight starts is the final fight. A fight still open when the mission ends ends with it",
    "public: a person of the city who is not security (one of the city's people who is not a guard, a patrol officer, an investigator or a watcher; the cast by role included, Vale in the Enforcer's hands not) stands on the street within `m` of the shooter of any of the fight's shots, line or no line (the reach that startles the crowd, crowd.scatter). Outside the final fight a fight's shots are those by or at the cell; in it, every shot. A fight nobody heard moves nothing",
    "it moves Standing once, when it ends, by the first outcome that holds; `none` moves nothing (rivals not feared who fired first, feared rivals not driven off, a withdrawal). fired-on: the cell fired, in this fight, on security (the guard, the patrol, the response's officers and robots, the final fight's officers) or on rivals (the rival crew, the final fight's ambush). rivals-public: the mission's rivals as the public sees them (site rivals.public, else fight.rivalsPublic). fired-first: the fight's first shot between the cell and the rivals was the cell's. rivals-broken: every rival body the cell fought in this fight (fired on or was fired on by; in the final fight, every rival of the ambush too) broke, was driven back or is down when it ends",
    "untraced shots count: Standing is the public's judgement, not evidence (fight.traced keeps the final fight's shots out of Trail and Alert only). A shot at a civilian is still violence (witness.sees, seen-violence) on top of the fight's move. A shot at anyone else (the guard, the rivals, officers) seen by a civilian keeps its witness Trail and Alert (violence seen: alert.violenceSeen) but no Standing of its own: its incident is traceable gunfire, and the fight judges it. A drawn weapon seen is still its own incident",
    "a fight is a seen act, not word: outside standing.word's cap; a move touches the district, so standing.drift skips it that mission"
   ],

Authority outranks everything, because a firefight with the police never reads as good; driving off a crew the district fears is the one fight that reads as good."

   "reason": "Sky 2026-10-16: turning conversations are private, which left nothing moving the city toward Hero; Motive's rule lets kindness (and harm, symmetrically) spread one hop through the person it was done to."
  },
  {
   "id": "standing.drift",
   "by": "city",
   "phase": "between-missions",
   "tag": "S",
   "src": "Sky 2026-10-16 (approved Motive's 'the benefit of the doubt'); briefs/014/motive-standing.md rule 5",
   "needs": [],
   "outcomes": [
    { "id": "moved", "when": [{ "k": "standing-moved", "is": true }], "changes": [{ "do": "debrief", "line": "standing" }] },
    { "id": "drifts", "when": [], "changes": [{ "do": "drift-standing", "step": "v:standing-drift", "to": "v:standing-start" }, { "do": "debrief", "line": "standing" }] }
   ],
   "how": [
    "per district, last in the phase so it sees every move: standing-moved holds when an act seen or found (in the mission, or a killing found after it: bodies.surface) or any word (standing.word, even one that nets to 0) touched the district this mission",
    "drift-standing moves the district at most `step` toward `to`, never past it: nothing at the start",
    "both outcomes write the district's one Standing line (debrief.lines.standing) with its cause from standing.causes"
   ],
   "proposed": true,
   "reason": "Motive: what the city stops seeing, it forgives; symmetric, so unkept Hero fades back to +2 as Menace does. Last in the phase (Motive had it after standing.word) so that a killing found between missions counts as a move."
  }
 ]
}

  "notes": [
    "Optimistic surface, coercive underneath (design intent, not a prompt line).",
    "Every district is retro-future (streamline, Googie, space age); no old-city stone or brick until Sky reopens it (2026-09-28).",
    "Prompt text fields (era, world, people, finishes.*.look, rules.*) are composed verbatim into prompts: keep them clean of meta.",
    "Migrated to the HML style contract v1 on 2026-10-06: kind lines and rules live under subjects; the cell inherit the people rules.",
    "Migrated to the HML style contract v2 on 2026-10-06 (v0.4.0): subjects, finishes and reference_board.groups became types, each owning its line, rules, finish, reference policy, brief fields and board. people became character (faction field: citizen, cell, security; the cell line and rules are the cell option, composed after the character line and rules, so the cell still inherit the people rules); world split into scene, building and backdrop; props, robots became prop, robot; nature is new. The v1 sheet finish serves character, prop, robot and nature; the plate finish serves scene, building and backdrop. The v1 explore finish (exploratory sheets and lineups: same world, lean brief, theme plus hard rules only, no motif lists; Codex, 1536x1024) is dropped as a finish; pass --model codex to style_probe.py for the free route. In v2 the prompt text fields are era, types.*.line, types.*.fields[].options[].line, types.*.finish.look, rules.all and types.*.rules: keep them clean of meta.",
    "2026-10-06 v0.4.1: nature board added (three picks generated from this spec in the studio with a borrowed prop reference); helmet added to negatives.",
    "v0.6.0 (2026-10-06): Sky: the style is meant to be simple, not down to the player or details. Types now set framing only; fields, faction options, cast rules and faction colours moved to contracts/style/suborned.brief-guide.json; v0.5.0 archived. Character style reference is a painted street plate first, because character images were copied as people.",
    "v0.6.1 (2026-10-06): the first v0.6.0 sheets came back as 1950s Americana (Sky: medium right, clothing and look all wrong). The couture sentence is the people's look, not a detail, so it is back on the character line; the era drops its dates, which pulled period dress.",
    "v0.6.2 (2026-10-06): v0.6.1 put every character in the same teal coat: 'bright coats' named one garment and the mint cafe_row plate set the colour. The line now asks for each outfit's own silhouette and colours; the character style plate is parade_eye (wider colour range, painted crowd).",
    "v0.7.0 (2026-10-06): Sky: v0.6.x 'still not the original look'. The look is the fashion vocabulary of the signed-off spaceage_bold sheets (workbench/Tools/Concept/citizens.py SPACEAGE + grounded medium), which is style, not cast control: restored on the character line and finish. 'helmet' negative removed (dome and helmet hats are the look; astronaut suit and space helmet stay out). Character style reference = the commuters spaceage_bold lineup (six people, so no single face is copied).",
    "v0.7.1 (2026-10-06): v0.7.0 put every motif on every person (dome helmet, cape, chevrons, teal vinyl on all three). The vocabulary is now a menu ('one or two of these, never all'); garments (tabards, bodysuits, jackets) come from the brief; capes removed and added to the negatives (Sky: capes no good).",
    "v0.7.2 (2026-10-06): v0.7.1 put a dome hat on all three test characters; Sky: hats 'sometimes'. The hat left the menu and became an occasional extra.",
    "v0.8.0 (2026-10-06): Sky wants six different characters on one sheet. New lineup type (2496x1664, six people in a row, three-quarter front view) from the original citizens.py LINEUP wording plus the same couture menu; character stays the single-person turnaround for modelling. Lineup style ref = the commuters spaceage_bold sheet.",
    "v0.8.1 (2026-10-06): Sky: make the number variable. The lineup line no longer fixes six: it takes the count from the brief ('Three couriers...', 'Ten shoppers...'), six when the brief gives none. No field: the number is content, so it lives in the brief.",
    "v0.8.2 (2026-10-06): the v0.8.0/v0.8.1 lineup tests both came back as a near pixel copy of the commuters spaceage_bold reference (cape included): Seedream treats a lineup reference on a lineup task as the image to reproduce. Lineup now sends no style image; the board stays as the look the text is judged against.",
    "v0.8.3 (2026-10-06): a count in the brief lost to the sheet ('Four dock workers' still drew six). The number is now a lineup field, People (2, 3, 4, 6, 8; default 6), whose option line states the exact count; the type line names no number.",
    "v0.8.4 (2026-10-06): Sky: keep costs low for now. Lineup size 2496x1664 -> 1536x1024: Seedream bills by resolution ($0.096 vs $0.048 per image).",
    "v0.8.5 (2026-10-06): 'White or silver boots' dropped from the character and lineup lines. v0.7.1 had pulled it out of the couture menu into its own sentence, so every figure wore them; footwear now comes from the brief.",
    "v0.8.6 (2026-10-06): Sky: 'Special ops / covert characters' came back as civilians. The character and lineup lines said 'everyday street clothing of a city'; now the look dresses whoever the brief names (civilian, worker, officer, agent) in what their role needs, role first, then one or two couture motifs. Lineup drops 'as in a real city' and the hat/coat/dress silhouette cues. The studio enhancer stopped treating the type line as the subject.",
    "v0.9.0 (2026-10-06): Sky: 'we've gone so far away from unique concept'; the style should feed the brief, not preset everything, and stay all in one. New hml.style/2 'guide' (global + per type), read only by Enhance as a menu: couture details, colours, cast, roles, factions, city, robots, nature (from the retired suborned.brief-guide.json, now archived). Character and lineup lines keep framing plus one couture sentence, so a plain brief still gets the look. Enhance stays manual.",
    "v0.9.1 (2026-10-06): the covert line ('blend into the crowd') sent Enhance straight back to civilians; agents and hard trades now read as what they are in sharper, darker couture. Lineup guide asks Enhance to describe each person in turn so no two share a detail.",
    "v0.9.2 (2026-10-06): v0.9.1 agents read as agents but the space age thinned to 80s/present-day leather and slip dresses; the agents line now keeps the couture details and only darkens the colour blocks.",
    "v0.9.3 (2026-10-06): v0.9.2 'one hot accent each' became a colour-coded squad in off-palette neon with matching glasses, earpieces and holsters. Agents now take darker blocks from the city palette. Sky: no references while a concept is being worked out. The studio enhancer now writes one numbered line per person when there are several (a group sentence lands on everyone), so the lineup's own guide line is dropped.",

    "v0.10.0 (2026-10-06): Sky: Make from Explore stayed too close to the sketch; it needs to move from explore to a finished design suitable for 3D model referencing. New type model (Model sheet): orthographic front, side and back on one baseline, neutral A-pose, flat even light, no cast shadows, finished painted rendering on light grey; no style image (the gouache board would pull it back to a sketch); a reference is treated as a rough concept, keeping the person and outfit, not its pose or rendering.",
    "v0.10.1 (2026-10-06): the model type is marked final: Explore does not propose it and Make on a one-person take uses it; the studio no longer matches it by name.",
    "v0.10.2 (2026-10-07): Sky: the type help was a long explainer. Every type's use line is now one short phrase.",
    "v0.11.0 (2026-10-07): Sky wants variations of the same character in a lineup; Lineup is different people and cannot keep one. New type versions: the same person drawn 2-6 times in a row, identical apart from the change the brief names; takes a subject reference (Edit this design).",
    "v0.11.1 (2026-10-07): update_url added: the studio checks it and offers 'Style vX is available' with one-click Update. Also tells the agent to propose one Versions take for several versions of one person.",
    "v0.11.2 (2026-10-07): Sky: every version kept the full-length coat although a shorter jacket had been asked for. The Versions type now lets the brief give a change for all figures (it replaces what the reference shows), not only per figure; the Explore agent restates standing changes in every brief.",
    "v0.11.3 (2026-10-07): Sky: Seedream 5.0 Pro dropped the chest plate and back harness when finishing a model sheet from a sketch; GPT Image 2 kept them. The Model sheet type now finishes with GPT Image 2.",
    "v0.17.0 (2026-10-12): Sky: presentation is 3D (the world is built from the plan, DecoKit plus procedural; painted plates at most an optional extra) and the world palette is a mix: pastel cream and peach base with saturated enamel accents, lagoon water, coral transit. palette_world records it from unity/Assets/Suborned/Editor/World/looks/harbour.json (sha256 in palette_world.source), current and tuneable. palette (the 6-colour mood set the concept tools compose from) is unchanged and still serves concept sheets for people and props. GDD v0.17.0 §15 is the art bible; the v0.15.0 html bible is history.",
    "v0.18.0 (2026-10-13): Sky (brief 007): signals render unlit and emissive, each with its shape or motion cue, and the deltaE2000 >= 20 gate applies to the unlit palette against the signal colours. palette_world re-recorded from looks/harbour.json (sha256 refreshed): water #2fc1de -> #3d8d93, trim #eadba6 -> #d0c848 (gold), new roles canvas #f7f4ec, accent_teal, accent_coral, accent_gold, accent_mint, accent_peach, accent_turquoise, accent_flamingo (the facade accent roles; no `accent` field, so tools/decokit mats.py ACCENT is unchanged) and beyond_ground, beyond_green, beyond_hill (horizon land). surface_overrides.gold_trim keeps #c9c08e only because the kit material DK_Gold17 reads it.",
    "v0.19.0 (2026-10-14): Sky (brief 008): the eight concept paintings of 2026-09-26 (briefs/008/concepts/, hashes in PROVENANCE.json) are the reference for the civic block and the district's street level; the skyline keeps the AtomicAge and Blocks sheets; the 30 Sep capstone concept is not the reference. Brass, not gold, at street level and on facades ('I prefer brass to gold'): roles.trim and roles.accent_gold #d0c848 -> #99784d (brass, deltaE2000 21.3 from guard); surface_overrides.gold_trim #c9c08e -> #99784d (no kit material reads it now: DK_Gold17 is light brass #ad866f, 21.3); new role crossing #d0c848 (the crossing landings' own surface, colour Sky's open pick, accent_mint #7fd0b8 recommended). Skyline crowns keep gold #e3d681 and #c9c08e as kit materials DK_Crown_Gold and DK_Crown_Gold17 (tools/decokit/mats.py; 20.6, 20.3), not palette roles.   "era": "Bright retro-future: a space age imagined as the present, built as high art, optimistic and immaculate.",
  "concept_prompt": {
    "era": "Optimistic atompunk city in an alternate history: a 1950s world that discovered atomic power centuries ago, so its culture and style are 1950s but its technology is centuries ahead: 1950s-styled robots, trams and street furniture doing super-advanced things. Atomic power made energy, travel and building cheap: sky rail, skyports, towers and liners, everything physical abundant. Thinking machines and networks never came: robots are clockwork-smart on fixed routines, and records are physical (microfilm, punch cards, pneumatic tubes, stamped forms). An abundant, orderly city that runs on routine and paperwork.",
    "city": "Streamline Moderne, Art Deco and Googie. Cream limestone and ivory enamel buildings with seafoam-teal faience bands, chrome sphere finials, banners on lamp posts, planted terraces, cypress and palms, parasol café terraces, pale cream stone paving with seafoam inlay bands, soft lilac-grey asphalt, thin brushed-brass hairline trim, coral and peach accents. Warm afternoon sun, soft shadows, soft blue sky. Clean, prosperous, graceful; people in the city's space-age couture. Cinematic painted concept art with photographic material realism.",

      "gold surfaces",
      "glass curtain walls",
      "grime",
      "text, signage lettering or words",
      "present-day street furniture",
      "1950s period dress: fedoras, trilbies, tea dresses, Americana"

    "people": "People in the city's space-age couture as everyday clothing: tailored, chic and wearable, the imagined future pushed one step further; never period costume.",
    "rule": "Every concept generation of a place, object or machine starts from this block (era, city, people, avoid) and an open brief: the art designs, and look decisions come from it. Checker rules gate what the art proposes; they are not the source of options. A decision taken from art cites the image and its prompt (PROVENANCE.json beside the images). Tools: Codex CLI image tool (ChatGPT plan), Runware (Qwen Image 2.1). People, character, lineup, model and versions prompts never take concept_prompt.era or any date: they start from the top-level era and the people's couture line (v0.6.1; Sky, 2026-10-14: 'too strong a 1950s ruined character concept'). People in a place frame are not costume reference.",

  },

  "guide": [
    "People wear space-age couture as everyday clothing: the imagined future of 1958-1972 pushed one step further. Any role, civilian, worker, officer or agent, wears it; the job shows through cut, colour and one telling detail (a slim chrome holster, an earpiece, a tool, a satchel), never through costume, tactical kit or matching uniforms.",
    "Couture details, one or two per person, never all, never the same pair twice on one sheet: visor glasses, a stand-up ribbed collar, glossy vinyl, bonded wool, silver lame or brushed-metal trim, a geometric cut-out, circles or chevrons, chunky geometric jewellery, a tabard over a fitted tunic, a transparent bubble umbrella or hatbox; only rarely a moulded dome or helmet hat. Garments and footwear follow the person.",
    "Colours on cream: seafoam teal, coral red, vermilion, mustard gold, white and silver, with navy and black for contrast; one dominant block per person, chosen for who they are, so a group never matches.",
    "Cast: mix ages, builds, genders and ethnicities unless the brief fixes them.",
    "Security and institutions dress sleeker: white, black, gold and chrome couture with armour accents.",
    "Agents, special ops and other hard trades read as what they are at a glance, still in the city's space-age couture: darker colour blocks from the city palette (navy, black, chrome, with coral, teal or gold) on the same details as everyone else, visor glasses, stand-up ribbed collars, glossy vinyl, geometric cuts, brushed-metal trim, and the tools of the trade worn like jewellery; never present-day leather, tactical kit or matching kit.",

   "reason": "Vantage: the office bay is a lay-by 3 m deep, carriageway level, outer edge on the kerb. Plan x -168.2..-153.8, y -310..-307. The Oct 9 source has no bay object (the ground is one flat floor), so the lay-by is stated here. Checker C-4."
  },
  {
   "op": "addBay", "id": "squareBay",
   "polygon": [[4, -50], [13, -50], [13, -47], [4, -47]],
   "reason": "Vantage: the square bay is a lay-by 3 m deep, carriageway level, outer edge on the kerb. Plan x -180..-177, y -243..-234. Not in the Oct 9 source. Checker C-4."
  },
  {
   "op": "addStructure",
   "item": { "id": "office-boarding-pavilion", "name": "Official door canopy", "category": "boarding-canopy", "polygon": [[75.5, -33], [78.5, -33], [78.5, -27], [75.5, -27]], "z": 4.05, "height": 0.57 },
   "reason": "Vantage, brief 008 B2 (L2; Sky's walk note 'parking bay goes into building'): the 15 x 3.827 pavilion at x 73.173..77 stood 2.327 x 6 m inside tower-official (x 69.5..75.5, y -33..-27). It is now a canopy carried on the tower's south face: back edge on the face (x 75.5, overlap 0), the tower's width (y -33..-27), 3 m out over the 1.5 m pavement and the kerb half of the lay-by (x 77..78.5). No posts: the pavement at the tower is 1.5 m and stays clear. z 4.05 is the soffit above the pavement (4.23 above the lay-by), top 4.62 as before; nothing of it stands on the ground. Why not the pavilion moved over the bay: a 15 m roof to x 80 hides the door from the play camera (yaw 30, pitch 38: at the door everything above 0.9 m), and its piers have no ground but the wide pavement or the lay-by. At 3 m a person at the door point (76.25, -30) is seen whole (hidden only above 2.0 m) and Vale is under cover from the door to the car door; 'Official drop-off' (78.2) and 'Boarding pavilion' (78.3) stay under it."
  },
  {
   "op": "addStructure",
   "item": { "id": "square-boarding-pavilion", "name": "Square bay canopy", "category": "boarding-canopy", "polygon": [[4.3, -47], [12.7, -47], [12.7, -44.858], [4.3, -44.858]], "z": 0, "height": 2.587 },
   "reason": "Vantage: as the office bay canopy; footprint 8.4 x 2.143 and height 2.587 from the Oct 5 testbed manifest, on the pavement edge at y -47."
  },
  { "op": "edit", "id": "office-pavilion-support-0", "move": [-2.3, 0], "z": 0, "height": 3.633, "reason": "Out of the lay-by onto the pavement (x 77.3..79.3 -> 75..77), z -0.18 -> 0, height cut by the 0.18. Brief 008 B2: the canopy is now carried on the tower and this pier carries nothing; it is removed by the pending `remove` below. Until that op exists it stays here, clear of the tower (y -37.75..-35.75) and of the bay." },
  { "op": "edit", "id": "office-pavilion-support-1", "move": [-2.3, 0], "z": 0, "height": 3.633, "reason": "As office-pavilion-support-0 (y -26.25..-24.25). Until it is removed it still overlaps the civic-office-north bed by about 0.7 x 1.6 m, as it did before." },
  { "op": "edit", "id": "square-pavilion-support-0", "move": [0, 1.16], "z": 0, "height": 1.955, "reason": "Supports follow the canopy out of the lay-by (y -48.16..-47.04 -> -47..-45.88, inside the canopy footprint); z -0.18 was the lay-by level, now they stand on the pavement, height cut by the 0.18 so the top stays where the source had it." },
  { "op": "edit", "id": "square-pavilion-support-1", "move": [0, 1.16], "z": 0, "height": 1.955, "reason": "As square-pavilion-support-0." },
  {
   "op": "addStructure",
   "item": { "id": "office-public-landing", "name": "Public door landing", "category": "entrance-landing", "polygon": [[61.7, -42], [66.3, -42], [66.3, -40.5], [61.7, -40.5]], "z": 0, "height": 0.75 },
   "reason": "Vantage, brief 008 B2 (L1, H4): steps are real geometry. Landing 1.5 m deep, 4.6 m wide, top at 0.75; sizes are Vela's RecordsEntrance. Sky 2026-10-19, door option (b), V-1 (briefs/011/vantage/study.ts optB; brief 023): the public door and its forecourt turn a quarter (from +x toward +y) off tower-public's north face onto the wing's west face, pivot (52.5, -30) -> (64, -40.5), front west onto Rocket Lane.
