{
  "schema": "suborned.plan/1",
  "id": "harbour-district",
  "name": "Harbour District",
  "version": "0.3.0",
  "date": "2026-10-14",
  "status": "transit from A04 run r008, accepted; world program brief 004; skyline and threaded sky rail brief 007 A; skyline text (why, crownWhy, conceptTiles, station kitWhy) from skyline run r011, accepted",
  "frame": { "units": "m", "x": "east", "y": "north", "origin": "Crown Circus centre", "unity": "(x, height, y)" },
  "sheet": {
    "drawing": "SBN-PLN-001",
    "x": [-400, 740],
    "y": [-780, 320],
    "grid": 100,
    "scale": "1:2500 @ A1",
    "inset": { "drawing": "SBN-PLN-002", "name": "Records Precinct", "x": [-236, 18], "y": [-428, -176], "scale": "1:500 @ A1" }
  },

  "standards": {
    "tram": { "radiusRunning": 50, "radiusLoop": 25, "stopSpacing": [300, 500], "platform": 30, "trackCentres": 3.6 },
    "skyrail": {
      "radiusLine": 70,
      "radiusLoop": 40,
      "spanStraight": 30,
      "spanCurve": 23,
      "spanTight": 18,
      "tightBelow": 180,
      "interchange": 150,
      "stationSpacing": [200, 500],
      "height": 24,
      "beamCentres": 6,
      "pylonZones": ["median", "mall", "park", "quay", "water", "island"],
      "pylonClear": {
        "tag": "[S]",
        "landmark": 3.8,
        "span": 36,
        "remnant": 0.5,
        "status": "Datum 2026-10-14: opt-in, key by key. landmark: derive keeps a pylon's centre this far outside every landmark disc (landmarks[].c, r). span: a span that crosses a landmark disc may be this long. remnant: no span next to a forced pylon (a landmark's edge, a portal's stand-off, the line's ends) is shorter than this fraction of its standard span. Absent, pylons are placed as before, so recorded runs rederive what they were made with. Splice, on Aster's call, 2026-10-14 (version kept at 0.2.0): landmark 0.8 → 3.8 (Latch's rebuild: the 0.8 left the pylon face 0.2 m off the basin rim), span 36 and remnant 0.5 added (the 0.8 left spans of 8.5 and 8 m)",
        "why": "Sky's walk of 2026-10-14, note 3, \"pillar in middle of steps\": S1/trunk's pylon at 6.5, 0 stood inside the Crown monument (landmarks.monument, r 14), whose basin and steps fill that disc: the CircusMonument piece is the orrery on a fluted column in a basin, 27.8 × 28.7 m (kitFit), r 6 → 14 = the basin, so walkers go round it in the garden ring. pylonZones said where a pylon may stand (the island is a disc r 24), not what else stands there. landmark 3.8 = half the pylon footprint (pylonSize 1.6 → 0.8) + streetscape keepClear.pylonFace 3: the face stands at least 3 m off the disc. The ground allows one pylon each side of the disc (island ring, r 24; x −44 to −24 and 24.5 to 43 along the trunk is not pylon ground), at −18 and 18 on the 0.5 m sample grid, so the beam crosses in one span of 36 m. span 36 = a deeper steel box beam over a landmark disc (Las Vegas monorail spans reach 36.6 m, Disney 33.5 m); S-P1/S-P2 take it as the limit for a span that crosses a disc only, everywhere else spanStraight / spanCurve / spanTight hold. remnant 0.5 = half the standard span (15 m): the pylons west of the monument are set again as equal spans on allowed ground (−83.5, −61.5, −45.5, −18: 22, 16, 27.5 m instead of 30, 30, 8.5 behind a pylon at −15), and the last pylon before a portal stands where the greedy left it when the pylon 3 m outside the jamb would leave a stub (5, 2 and 12 m at Space HQ, the Parade gate and the Skyport: the building carries the beam from its jamb). The terminus stub past the Skyport portal (570 to 575) stays: both its pylons are forced. SF-18 (a pylon's footprint clears steps, landmarks, bays, buildings; 2 m from crossings and doorways) checks the export"
      },
      "beamUnderside": 21.5,
      "beamUndersideWhy": "[S] height 24 − 1.0 (car floor over beam top, Alweg straddle) − 1.5 (beam depth, Seattle 1962). SF-4 (tree canopies ≥ 5 m from the beam envelope) and levels.headroom.underBeam measure from it; streetscape.skyrailEnvelope.underside repeats it",
      "portal": {
        "tag": "[S]",
        "rule": "brief 007 (Sky 2026-10-13): the sky rail threads buildings. A building or megastructure may stand over or around the line only at a declared portal (signatures[].portal, megastructures[].portals, megastructures[].supports.portal). Inside a portal the structure carries the beam (no pylon needed), and nothing of it stands inside the opening below its soffit",
        "running": {
          "twin": { "clearHalfWidth": 6.0, "z": [21.5, 29.0] },
          "single": { "clearHalfWidth": 4.0, "z": [21.5, 29.0] },
          "why": "opening 12.0 × 7.5 (twin) / 8.0 × 7.5 (single), grammar §8 (Vela): beam centres ±3 (beamCentres 6) + half car 1.65 (SkyRail_Car 3.3 wide) + 1.35 clear = 6.0; sill at the beam underside 21.5 (beamUnderside), head 29.0 = car top 27.4 (grammar §8) + 1.6 for the current collector and the arched head. The building's floors at 24 run to the jambs (levels.list concourse)"
        },
        "station": {
          "clearHalfWidth": 16,
          "soffit": 30,
          "why": "a station inside a building: platforms to skyrailEnvelope.half 3.75 + 4 = 7.75 from the line (levels.station), + concourse minWidth 8 = 15.75 → 16 (the Skyport Tower's legs, supports.portal.clearHalfWidth 16); soffit 30 = the Skyport portal frame soffit (megastructures.skyport-tower.frame [30, 34]), ≥ 24 + headroom.walk 3 with room for the platform canopy"
        },
        "pylons": "inside a portal the beam bears on the building (portal sills and the station hall floor); outside it S-P1 and S-P2 hold unchanged",
        "source": "brief 007 · contracts/world/harbour-district.grammar.md §8 · Blocks/rail_through.png · AtomicAge/monorail_terminal.png · EPCOT (1966): the monorail through the Cosmopolitan Hotel's transportation lobby"
      }
    },
    "transit": { "reach": 250, "onLine": 3 },
    "skyline": {
      "tag": "[S]",
      "rule": "brief 007 (Sky 2026-10-13): one dominant icon, a cluster of rival spires, crowns everywhere. The plan makes sites for the signature structures (signatures[], towers.sites, landmarks); scale, levels, clearances and the checker still rule how they stand",
      "dominant": { "id": "space-hq", "tip": 252, "why": "SpaceHQ as built (kit 252.0 tall): the tallest thing in the district (Sky 2026-10-13); every other tip stays under rivalMax" },
      "rivalMax": 200,
      "rivalMaxWhy": "≤ 0.8 × dominant (201.6), rounded down: the dominant stays at least a quarter taller than its tallest rival, as SpaceHQ over the needle trio in Blocks/needle_trio.png and mixed_skyline.png. The rival cluster sits 0.45–0.8 of the dominant",
      "harbour": { "icon": "skyport-tower", "tip": 108, "within": 150, "why": "the Skyport Tower stays the harbour's icon (brief 007 Fixed): nothing standing within 150 m of the quay edge (x 312) tops 108; the rival spires stand inland, north of Crown Circus" },
      "tiers": [
        "dominant 252: space-hq (signatures)",
        "rival spires 120–200: avenue-starburst 194.3, avenue-needle 167.8, avenue-gate-w / -e 165.6 (DiscTower pair + SkyBridge), crescent-terrace 122.7",
        "harbour icon 108: skyport-tower; under it on the water liner-berth 103.7 (its terminal tower) and the ocean-liner 34.0 alongside, and the harbour front (harbour-hotel 106, crescent-tower 99.4, parade gates 75)",
        "marks 80–106: skylon 100, sphere 80, lantern-beacon 86.1",
        "street wall 20–50: H(4)–H(12), every building ≥ 9 storeys crowned (grammar §6)"
      ],
      "crowns": "every tower and signature names its crown: the signature pieces keep their own (SpaceHQ atom over a needle mast; Tower_Needle needle and saucers; Tower_Starburst starburst; DiscTower disc, jib and mast; Tower_Terrace belvedere finial; Skylon spindle); tower sites take the grammar §6 catalogue (contracts/world/harbour-district.grammar.md); within 150 m no two towers share a crown type, matched pairs excepted",
      "source": "brief 007 · Blocks/needle_trio.png, mixed_skyline.png, saucer_spires.png, skyport_tower.png · AtomicAge/exposition_palace.png, power_spire.png · grammar §6"
    },
    "horizon": {
      "sea": "water[0] ends at the sheet edge (x 740): it is the playable water and the sheet's frame, not the sea's edge. The world export derives the visual sea plane (16 × 16 km about Crown Circus, the plan water's surface, colour and swell) and the horizon band beyond the district (grammar §9); no plan geometry, nothing playable past x 740",
      "meets": "the visual sea joins water[0] along x 740 and y −780 / 320 at the same surface level; the band's rings stand ≥ 150 m outside the outermost plan footprint (grammar §9), so nothing of it lands inside the sheet",
      "source": "brief 007 C · grammar §9 (Vela) · Horizon/pano/pano_harbour.png"
    },
    "roads": { "junctionSpacing": { "primary": 250, "district": 60 }, "frontage": 1 },
    "walking": {
      "crossAnywhere": true,
      "grid": 2,
      "directness": 1.5,
      "from": ["Café door", "Office entrance"],
      "note": "Players cross any road anywhere: carriageways, kerbs, medians, the tram reservation and the circus are walkable ground. Only buildings, built plots, landmarks and water block. Crossings are traffic calming and dressing, never the only way over.",
      "body": {
        "tag": "[S]",
        "r": 0.65,
        "rWhy": "the clearance a walker keeps from a ground solid (wall, cheek, pilaster, planting bed, table, fountain, pillar, cabinet, monument) when a walk is measured: one value fits both walks Waymark measured in the game (Crew line → Between tables 26.2 m, Service lane → Office entrance 25.5 m; 0.65 gives 26.1 and 25.5). A walker is 2r = 1.3 m wide with it. Was the constant BODY in tools/plan/walk-solids.ts; the dressing's own scratch check used 0.35 and the Unity NavMesh agent is radius 0.5, both inside it",
        "clearWidth": 2.0,
        "constrained": { "w": 1.5, "run": 6 },
        "aisle": 1.3,
        "ends": 1.5,
        "widthWhy": "clear width = the free width between two ground solids, or a solid and a building, tower, built plot or water, measured square across the walk. 2.0 m lets two people (two wheelchairs) pass and equals the access section's walk zone (sections.access.walk), so a dressed block is held to the street's own figure; 1.5 m where a fixed thing leaves no more, for at most 6 m of the walk (Inclusive Mobility's acceptable minimum and its length of restricted width); a seating area (a café or bar terrace inside its own wall, rail or planter line: the CafeBay terrace) keeps aisles of 2r = 1.3 m, the width of one walker, and its gate keeps clearWidth (the terrace gate is 5.2). A gap of 2r or less is closed: no walk passes it. Within `ends` of a door, a seat or a Handover point the width is not judged (a door in its reveal, a chair at its table). Streets already hold more: the walk zones of every section (SF-1: access 2, district and primary 3, mall and walk 4) and the deck clearMin",
        "measured": "2026-10-15 (Datum), civic block /4 with its dressing, 39 points (the 3 doors; the 25 Handover points of contracts/missions/handover/mission.json, 20 where they are not a door; the 16 crossing landings round the block), 741 walks on a 0.2 m grid: at a 1.5 m clear width no walk is cut off or longer than at r; at 2.0 m none is cut off and 62 are longer by more than 2 m (all of them into the café terrace or to the Fountain point beside its basin). Of the 47 gaps under 2.0 m on the block's ground, walks pass through 4, all inside the café terrace: 1.85 m between cafe-table-1 or -2 and the terrace wall, 1.36 m between cafe-table-6 and cafe-palm-5 and between cafe-table-4 and cafe-palm-4 (aisles ≥ 1.3: pass). Outside the terrace no walk passes a gap under 2.0 m",
        "source": "DfT, Inclusive Mobility (2021) §3.1, as quoted by the IDGO street design guide (openspace.eca.ed.ac.uk/resources/idgo-design-guides/the-design-of-streets-with-older-people-in-mind/widths-of-footways-and-footpaths): 2000 mm so two wheelchairs pass, 1500 mm where constraints prevent it, 1000 mm absolute at an obstacle; Manual for Streets (2007): 2000 mm unobstructed in lightly used streets; Reigate & Banstead pavement licence guidance (reigate-banstead.gov.uk, pavement licensing): 1500 mm clear between tables and chairs and the footway edge, after Inclusive Mobility §3.1"
      },
      "rules": [
        { "id": "W-5", "tag": "[S]", "if": "on a block with ground solids (civic.solids): (a) a walk the plan checker (W-1, W-2), the people checker (P-1) or a mission draws passes within body.r of a ground solid, or a step is tested against cell centres instead of the solids' own edges; (b) a walk passes a gap narrower than body.clearWidth, except a gap of at least body.constrained.w over no more than body.constrained.run of the walk, or an aisle of at least body.aisle inside a seating area; within body.ends of a door, seat or Handover point nothing is judged", "why": "planters, tables and furniture never pinch a walk; one body for every walk the game measures, on any grid (the people's 2 m grid ignores the block's solids today)", "owner": "Splice: the checker rule; walk-solids.ts and tools/people/walk.ts read body.r from here; the block declares its seating areas (Vantage), until then the CafeBay terrace (between the café and its terrace wall) is the one" }
      ]
    },

When Inez calls, the guard stops at her free side: the first of the rounds file's guard.stops with nobody within partners-clear-cm (100 cm, proposed [S]) at the call. No script changed: all 36 keep outcome, end tick, cash, Trail and Alert; every final hash moves (inputs 1101841386259720413 -> 13665962258232316490: the rulebook and the rounds file are inputs); every condition and every slack row is as c020. In fail-entry-seen-camera and fail-entry-seen-patrol the Scout is at beside-inez at the call and the guard stands 151 cm from him (0.8.0: 90 cm, between him and Inez), the Fixer 278 cm off; fail-entry-seen-guard never calls. beside-inez does not move. Correction to c020's note (route A's spare time is not 8-12 s): that slack is the checker shifting the steps before the call (0:00 to 1:59) late, so a scripted order lands while Inez is on a round and is refused; a player would wait for her. Route A's spare time is the call's (Pulse, brief 022 §7.2, measured again on 0.8.1): with the Tech's Reroute as recorded (1:14.5) the call can slip 92 s and still win (93 s fails entry-seen-patrol); about 129 s clean if the Tech is retimed with it (the script shifted from the Listen with the Reroute moved plays 5 T, A 1 to 129 s late, call 4:58.5, wherever the scripted Listen is taken), and it wins to 175 s, until Vale has gone. sim/Suborned.Sim/Suborned.Sim.csproj.text:
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <!-- The Suborned's one simulation engine (GDD §11, brief 011 A, Keel): a Unity-free class library. netstandard2.1 so Unity loads
       the same DLL; no package references, so nothing but this code decides a run. Integer state, 10 Hz, replay = orders + checksums. -->
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>netstandard2.1</TargetFramework>
    <LangVersion>9.0</LangVersion>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <RootNamespace>Suborned.Sim</RootNamespace>
    <AssemblyName>Suborned.Sim</AssemblyName>
    <Deterministic>true</Deterministic>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>false</GenerateDocumentationFile>
    <!-- Redline E9: overflow throws in Debug (the tests); wrap-around code says unchecked. E10: the same source gives the same DLL bytes on every machine. -->
    <CheckForOverflowUnderflow Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">true</CheckForOverflowUnderflow>
    <PathMap>$(MSBuildProjectDirectory)=/_/Suborned.Sim/</PathMap>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- brief 025: recorded sessions the scenarios replay (DP1), embedded so Unity's player replays them as the CLI does -->
    <EmbeddedResource Include="Fixtures/*.json" LogicalName="Suborned.Sim.Fixtures.%(Filename)%(Extension)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <!-- The engine headless (brief 011 A): play a scenario or an order script; prints outcome, event log and checksums, for bun and people. -->
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <AssemblyName>suborned-sim</AssemblyName>
    <RootNamespace>Suborned.Sim.Cli</RootNamespace>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup><ProjectReference Include="../Suborned.Sim/Suborned.Sim.csproj" /></ItemGroup>
</Project>
